chapters.title: How to Read This Manual

blocks.text: How to read

This is a fan-made field guide, laid out like the paper manuals that used to come in the box. Grand Theft Auto VI came out on 19 November 2026. Most of the manual was first written before then; it has now been rewritten for the released game, and it is still careful about what it claims.

blocks.caption: Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, the two leads, on the waterfront.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason and Lucia 01"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Every statement about how the game works carries a small label saying where it comes from. Read the label before you rely on the sentence. Where the published sources disagree, the manual gives both instead of picking a winner.

blocks.title: Verified
blocks.text: Seen in Rockstar's own material: the trailers, the screenshots and website, the Extended Look video, and Rockstar's support articles. This is the firmest ground the manual has.

blocks.title: Developer-described and preview-reported
blocks.text: What Rockstar's Rob Nelson said in interviews, and what journalists and creators reported from Rockstar's preview, all before launch. These are kept wherever the launch sources have not contradicted them.

blocks.title: Reported at launch
blocks.text: What reviews and guides written from the released game report. Nobody working on this manual has checked these in play, and many figures come from a single guide. When a pre-launch statement has been confirmed or corrected at launch, both appear together and the label shows the newer evidence.

blocks.title: Verified after release
blocks.text: Kept for statements checked against the released game by the people writing this manual. Nothing carries it yet.

blocks.caption: The game's illustrated cover art, from Rockstar's launch-day post: Jason and Lucia in the centre panel, other characters, vehicles and an alligator around them.

blocks.text: Nothing in this manual is official. It is an unofficial fan guide, not made or approved by Rockstar Games.
Spoilers and
The game is out, so the manual now holds things players only found by playing it. Those are covered until you choose to see them.

blocks.title: What counts as a spoiler
blocks.text: Anything known before launch is shown plainly: the trailers, Rockstar's screenshots and website, the Extended Look video, interviews and previews. Anything learned only from the released game is a spoiler, however small.

blocks.title: How spoilers are hidden
blocks.text: Spoiler sentences are blurred where they stand, and so are pictures taken from the released game. Choose to see spoilers and they come into view. Titles are always written so they give nothing away on their own.

blocks.caption: A phone home screen in the released game. Pictures like this stay blurred until you choose to see spoilers.

blocks.title: No story plot
blocks.text: Missions are described by who gives them, where they start and what they pay or unlock. How the story unfolds and how it ends are left for you to find.

blocks.title: The Encyclopedia holds the full lists
blocks.text: The manual explains how things work. Every vehicle, weapon, store, mission, animal and collectible has its own entry in the app's Encyclopedia, with its sources. Where an item in the manual has an entry, its title is a link, and Open the full entry takes you there.

blocks.title: What is still unknown
blocks.text: Boxes marked Unknown list what the sources read do not settle. They shrink as more is published.

blocks.text: Getting started:
What the game puts on screen. Rockstar's pre-release footage showed most of it; launch guides now say what the bars and icons are and add the map.

blocks.caption: A shootout in an office: two bars at the top left, ammunition and the weapon at the top right.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 25:16

blocks.title: Wanted stars and Heat icons
blocks.text: Top right. Up to six stars, with a row of small red icons beneath showing what the police know. The Law Enforcement chapter covers both.

blocks.title: Ammunition and weapon
blocks.text: Under the stars: two numbers and the outline of the weapon in hand. In one firefight they read 40 and 250, then 34 and 221, then 20 and 205 as the shooting goes on.
blocks.frameAlt: Four white stars, four red icons, the numbers 40 and 250, and the outline of a rifle
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:12

blocks.title: Bars at the top left
blocks.text: In a late shootout in the footage: a pink bar with a heart, and under it a purple bar with an eye. ||Launch guides name three stats behind the bars: the pink heart is Strength (health), a lightning bolt is Cardio (stamina) and the purple eye is Focus. PowerPyx and Push Square call the lightning green, GameSpot blue. Push Square says pressing Down on the D-pad shows all three, and PowerPyx says body armour adds a blue bar above health.|| The next page covers them.

blocks.title: Minimap
blocks.text: Bottom left: a rounded panel with buildings drawn in three dimensions, an arrow for you, a north marker on its edge, and, with a destination set, a pink route line and the distance. ||PowerPyx says the minimap can be set to appear only when Down on the D-pad is pressed.||
blocks.frameAlt: A rounded minimap with a three-dimensional building, a pink route line and a distance of 1.86 miles
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 8:20

blocks.title: The minimap while wanted, and the fruit bowl
blocks.text: During a police chase the minimap is tinted blue in some frames and red in others. A small fruit-bowl icon sits in its top-left corner in most gameplay frames.
blocks.frameAlt: A blue-tinted minimap with a small fruit-bowl icon in its top-left corner
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:12

blocks.title: Prompts
blocks.text: Small prompts appear at the bottom right for what you can do at that moment. "Smoke" and "Throw" can be read in the footage.

blocks.title: The map and its index
blocks.text: ||The touchpad (View on Xbox) opens the map. Right on the D-pad opens its index, in nine tabs: Personal, Story, Robberies, Activities, Exploration, Vehicles, Weapons, Style and Food. Newly found entries carry an orange diamond, and only one destination can be active at a time; Square drops extra markers (GamesRadar+). PowerPyx says shops appear only once the fog over their area has cleared, and hovering over an icon shows details such as an Ammu-Nation's stock tier.||

blocks.caption: The pause-menu map of an island town, with the index icons down the left, the tabs Jason & Lucia, Map, Brief and Progress across the top, and two money figures at the top right.

items: What the fruit-bowl icon on the minimap means. No source read explains it.

blocks.text: Health,
Rockstar said before launch that eating matters and that your body changes with what you do. Launch guides describe three stats, a handful of healing items and a Fitness app that keeps count.

blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 25:16 and 25:22

frames.alt: A full pink bar with a heart icon, split in two, above a full purple bar with an eye icon
frames.label: About 25:16, both full

frames.alt: The pink heart bar full and the purple eye bar about a quarter full
frames.label: About 25:22, eye bar draining

blocks.title: Three stats
blocks.text: The footage shows a pink heart bar, divided in two by a marker, above a purple eye bar. TGG reported three bars from Rockstar's preview: health, stamina and Focus. ||Launch guides agree: Strength sets maximum health, Cardio sets maximum stamina, and Focus sets how long Combat Focus lasts. DayOne's review and PowerPyx say each runs to level 4, and IGN says Jason starts with Strength at level 3. The two leads are tracked separately, so training as one does nothing for the other (IGN).||

blocks.caption: The Fitness app's stat screen.

blocks.title: Eating
blocks.text: Rob Nelson told IGN that eating has quite a dramatic effect on your health and gives a substantial buff. In Famitsu's interview, read in translation, he says a food buff lifts a gauge beyond its normal maximum, and that the extra is lost once life falls below normal. ||GameSpot says food and drink marked with a pink heart restore health up to the maximum, and those with an orange heart push it above the maximum for a while; buffs from eating, sleeping and showering last for the play session or until the lead dies. PowerPyx advises eating or drinking at the start of each in-game day.||

blocks.title: Where food comes from
blocks.text: In IGN's demo Jason takes a drink from the safehouse fridge. TGG reports goods picked off a convenience store shelf, a drive-thru order that gave a temporary boost, and a vending machine at a gym; IGN's writers saw food marked with a heart or a lightning bolt. ||PowerPyx says fast food stores, cafes and takeouts, street food vendors and liquor stores sell food that boosts stats for a while, and convenience stores sell groceries for the fridge at home. IGN says apples, free in many receptions and kitchens or $1 in stores, and vending-machine snacks are the commonest healing foods.||

blocks.title: Healing items
blocks.text: ||Zombix restores half your health and is used with L1 and Square (LB and X), says PowerPyx. IGN prices it at $15 a bottle at convenience stores and says each lead carries up to five. Adrenaline gives a bigger boost, turns the bars gold for a short time and lengthens Combat Focus; PowerPyx puts it on L1 and Triangle (LB and Y). PowerPyx says both are sold at convenience stores, while IGN says Adrenaline cannot be bought, is found in first aid and trauma kits, and that three can be carried. IGN says hospitals hold both for free.||

blocks.caption: The weapon and item wheel, with an arrow pointing at the Zombix bottle and the adrenaline shot in the bottom-left corner.

blocks.title: Health coming back
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says health comes back slowly if you take no damage, but only up to a solid white line on the bar, and more slowly when stamina is low. IGN says that line moves up with workout gains. Healing items used again and again in one fight work a little less each time (GameSpot). Body armour, bought at Ammu-Nation, adds its own blue bar and is refilled only with a new vest (PowerPyx).||

blocks.title: Stamina
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says an energy drink strengthens the stamina gauge, that stamina drains with each movement of a workout, and that its base level rises with training. TGG reports that in water the stamina bar becomes a lung-capacity meter. ||IGN says Cardio rises a little from sprinting in ordinary play. GameSpot mentions separate lung and oxygen gauges without explaining them.||

blocks.title: The eye bar is Focus
blocks.text: In the office shootout the purple bar drains from full to empty in about fourteen seconds, from 25:10 to 25:24. Nelson compared Focus to Eagle Eye before launch. ||IGN says Focus starts with a click of both sticks, lasts 30 seconds on foot and drains only while you aim or shoot. Push Square and GameSpot say Focus gains are permanent, while Strength and Cardio slip back if neglected. Fighting with it is covered in Weapons & Equipment.||

items: Whether sprinting drains stamina, and what happens when it runs out.
||What most food costs and how much can be carried. The guides read give prices only for Zombix and apples.||

blocks.text: Body, sleep
The gym, the bed and the safehouse. Nelson told TGG before launch that the story can be finished without managing any of it; launch guides describe how it works when you do.

blocks.title: Joining a gym
blocks.text: In the demo TGG saw, Jason and Lucia first signed up at a front desk, with changing rooms and a vending machine nearby. ||Game Rant names Venus Fitness in Vice City, with a $600 membership. PowerPyx says the first house has weights on its terrace, and Game Rant mentions a free punching bag under Jason's house. When the two go to a gym together, the lead you are not playing works out too (PowerPyx, GameSpot).||

blocks.title: The workout ring and its window
blocks.text: TGG saw three exercises fill a ring and give a temporary boost: strength work for health, cardio for stamina. ||The Fitness app sets a workout window for Strength and one for Cardio. Fill the ring to the day's white dash, then rest and sleep before the window reopens; miss a window and that stat slips back (Push Square, IGN). Strength work uses both triggers, as in bench presses, deadlifts and chest flys; cardio machines are a timing game. An unfinished workout gives nothing, and a protein shake or bar straight afterwards shortens the wait for the next window.||

blocks.caption: The Fitness app's workout window rings.

blocks.title: Eat first
blocks.text: Stamina was low when Nelson went in. A coffee or an energy drink beforehand gives a stamina boost that makes the workout easier. ||IGN adds that Strength gains suffer if the lead is hungry or tired.||

blocks.title: Body shape
blocks.text: Nelson told IGN that overeating puts on weight and that gyms raise muscle or strength. TGG relayed other previews that the menu shows body fat, muscle and sleep quality. ||Push Square says the Fitness app tracks Hunger and a Body Composition of muscle and body fat that decides how the lead looks. Eating too much brings a Calorie Surplus message and weight gain after sleeping; protein shakes with steady workouts bring a Calorie Deficit. Game Rant says the lead needs food after a full workout to gain size.||

blocks.title: Sleep and the clock
blocks.text: TGG relayed that a lead who has not slept gets bags under the eyes, and said a day lasts longer than in Grand Theft Auto V. ||The bed at home offers four wake times: Morning (7:00 AM), Noon (12:30 PM), Evening (6:00 PM) and Night (12:01 AM). PowerPyx timed an in-game minute at 6 real seconds, so a full day lasts 2 hours 24 minutes. Sleeping starts the next workout window, and DayOne's review says the leads need sleep every few days.||

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia lying together on a bed at home.

blocks.title: Home comes with the story
blocks.text: The safehouse changes as chapters pass, and you cannot buy more of them; garages are what you buy. Inside, TGG says, you can switch lights, eat, shower, shave or cut your hair, watch television and sleep. ||GameSpot says each chapter is built around a different home, and an earlier one can be visited again only from an older save. PowerPyx lists a bed, a wardrobe for bought clothes and a fridge for protein shakes and groceries, and says washing your face or showering gives a short Focus boost. TheSixthAxis's review confirms garages are the only property for sale.||

blocks.caption: Jason's first safehouse, with its exercise deck and jetty.

blocks.title: Hair and looks
blocks.text: A barber can take you from short hair straight to a longer style; at home you can only shorten it. ||PowerPyx counts 18 hair and beauty salons. All sell the standard styles and some add their own, and in beauty salons Lucia can also change nail colour and makeup. Bought clothes are put on at the wardrobe at home, in a store's changing room or from clothes kept in a car's trunk. DayOne's review says a new haircut helps shed police recognition.||

items: ||Whether hair grows back by itself in the released game. TGG was told before launch that it does not; no launch source read says either way.||

blocks.text: Jason and Lucia:
You play both. Rob Nelson described how they share the game before launch; launch guides add the buttons and the limits.

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia standing side by side in a dim room, both holding guns.

blocks.title: Switching
blocks.text: Nelson said the team kept switching as open as possible, though the story sometimes rules it out. In the Extended Look the swap is instant when the two are together and takes a few seconds when they are apart. ||PowerPyx, Push Square and GamesRadar+ give the input as hold Right on the D-pad and press R1 (RB); GameSpot says L1 (LB). PowerPyx says free switching begins after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, with only Jason playable for most of Chapter 1; GameSpot puts it at about 30 percent of the story. After that, TheSixthAxis's review says, you can switch whenever a mission does not need one of them.||

blocks.title: The other one carries on
blocks.text: The lead you are not playing keeps a routine, sometimes at the safehouse and sometimes out, Nelson said. ||TheSixthAxis's review says switching puts you with the other lead somewhere else in the world, rarely in the middle of something. A darkened portrait means the partner is busy for now, and a J or L on a mission's map icon means only that lead can play it (GamesRadar+). Push Square's review says each lead has activities of their own, and GameSpot says the one you are not playing usually stays near the current home.||

blocks.caption: Lucia and Jason walking side by side along a street, seen from behind.

blocks.title: Calling the other one over
blocks.text: Nelson said that when you switch seats in a car, the other drives. ||Hold Right and press Triangle (Y) to invite the other lead, who arrives at about the same time as you; the same input splits the pair up again (Push Square, PowerPyx). Together, the partner can be asked to drive your personal vehicle and speed up or slow down, to wait in the car or come in as backup, or to take the car away (GamesRadar+). Focusing on the partner with L2 (LT) starts a conversation and lets you share food and drink.||

blocks.title: Passing bags
blocks.text: ||Each lead carries two stash bags. Hold Right, press Circle (B) and choose Hand Over Bag to pass one (PowerPyx). A partner sent off with the loot can sell it to a fence alone, possibly for less, and the money arrives later (GamesRadar+, GameSpot).||

blocks.title: Two of everything
blocks.text: TGG reported that each lead has their own phone, their own stats and their own criminal profile. ||Launch guides agree, and add a personal bank account for each (GamesRadar+); the Fitness app tracks the two separately (IGN).||
The
Each lead has a phone of their own, seen held in the hand while you use it. Launch guides name about a dozen apps, several of them installed by story missions.

blocks.caption: Jason Duval leaning against a tree on a lit street at dusk, holding a phone.

blocks.title: Taking it out
blocks.text: ||Up on the D-pad brings the phone out without pausing the game, and it works while driving; with it out in a vehicle, you drive in first person (Game Rant, GameSpot, PowerPyx). A Reminders list, opened with Up then Square (X), gathers messages awaiting a reply, news stories and Snapmatic posts (Push Square).||

blocks.caption: ||The apps named by launch guides, mostly from Game Rant's list and IGN's guide. GameSpot calls the messaging app Messages.||
rows: ||Texts. Messages can carry photos and map coordinates; a red dot marks unread ones||
||Calls, including Paradise Taxi from the first mission on||
||The bank account and payments; set up in the Chapter 1 mission Buck Me||
||Hunger, the workout window and each stat's level||
||The phone camera, with a selfie mode; Gallery is listed beside it||
||Stories from The Leonida Journal, Weazel News and the Vice City Horn; a two-day forecast with sunset times||
||Delivers your personal vehicle; installed after the Chapter 2 mission Moses||
||Sells garages; arrives shortly after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver||
||Wallpapers and ringtones, and later plugins such as the Cop Scanner and the Key Cloner||

blocks.caption: The phone's home screen with its standard apps.

blocks.title: The scanner
blocks.text: Nelson described holding the phone over a vehicle to learn whether it is locked, alarmed or tracked, what it is worth to a Pay n' Spray or a car fence, and what registering it would cost. ||The app is WAiNK. PowerPyx says it can be raised without opening the phone by holding Up, and GamesRadar+ says R1 (RB) then scans. TheSixthAxis's review describes the same readout: sale value, registration fee, and whether the car has a tracker or keyless entry.||

blocks.title: Snapmatic and the news
blocks.text: You follow people on Snapmatic and can browse it. Nelson says the pair never post, being on the run: they just lurk. ||PowerPyx says checking Snapmatic and News sometimes marks places on the map.||

blocks.title: Rides instead of fast travel
blocks.text: In IGN's demo the pair travelled by a ride app IGN compared to Uber. ||PowerPyx says there is no fast travel from the map itself. Paradise Taxi, in the phone's contacts from the first mission, takes you to any marked destination, and a flat $100 on top of the fare skips the ride. RydeMe arrives in Chapter 2: a driver turns up within seconds, the fare rises with distance and $100 skips the drive. GamesRadar+ says Paradise Taxi takes pocket cash and RydeMe the bank balance; a skipped ride moves the clock on by the length of the drive.||

blocks.title: Waypoints
blocks.text: Nelson says holding Down on the D-pad is a quick way to set a waypoint. ||Launch guides call this Quick Navigation: hold Down to show nearby shops and missions in the world, then press R3 on a marker to set a route to it.||

blocks.title: Music on foot
blocks.text: ||There is no radio app. Buy headphones at an electronics store, marked by a headphone icon, and hold Left on the D-pad outside a vehicle to open the station list; Down moves to podcasts (GameSpot). GameSpot prices over-ear headphones at about $200 and in-ear at $119, and IGN names Zeke's Gadgets in Hamlet as the store nearest the start.||

blocks.caption: The map with the Style > Electronics list open and the info card for Zekes Gadgets.

blocks.title: The camera
blocks.text: ||Game Rant says the rear camera has a grid, zoom up to 5x and 17 filters, and the front camera offers up to six poses, seven expressions and a pose with your partner.||
Cash, bank
Nelson says money matters more in this story than in earlier games. Where it is kept decides what you lose when things go wrong. Earning it is covered in Money & Businesses and Robberies & Stealing.

blocks.caption: A pistol and a submachine gun with a blue palm-leaf pattern on a car's back seat, beside a duffel bag and stacks of cash.

blocks.title: Three figures
blocks.text: TGG reports a bank balance, the cash you are carrying, and the value of loot you have not sold; loot in a duffel bag shows as its own figure. ||Push Square says pressing Down on the D-pad shows both balances.||

blocks.title: BuckMe, the bank
blocks.text: Before launch the banking app was only heard, as "Buck Me". ||The app is BuckMe, set up in the Chapter 1 mission Buck Me, and each lead has their own BuckMe Checking account (GamesRadar+). Purchases come out of the bank even with no cash on you. Pocket cash covers only items up to $1,000; anything dearer must be paid through the app (PowerPyx, GamesRadar+).||

blocks.title: Cash in your pocket and ATMs
blocks.text: Banked money is safe and carried cash is not; Nelson told TGG that depositing cash means going to an ATM. ||Each lead can carry up to $20,000. At an ATM, Triangle (Y) offers Deposit, Withdraw and recent transactions, up to $20,000 at a time, and the ATM Finder at the bottom of BuckMe routes you to the nearest machine (GamesRadar+, Push Square). IGN advises banking cash as soon as BuckMe is set up, along with any cash stashed in the safehouse bedroom.||

blocks.caption: A phone held up on a Vice City street, showing the BuckMe app with a Premium badge, a $2M goal, the ATM Finder and questions about limits and Family Savings.

blocks.title: Account limits
blocks.text: ||Rockstar Support says the BuckMe Checking and Family Savings accounts have limits that rise only as the main story moves on, and that payments held up by a full Checking account go through once it is upgraded. It gives no figures.||

blocks.title: Family Savings
blocks.text: ||The two leads share a Family Savings account. PowerPyx says money put in is gone for good, even after the story, but investing is needed to raise the checking limit. GameSpot says its goals bring better interest and strengthen the relationship; IGN puts the first milestone at $5,000, and DayOne's review says each chapter's target pays a reward. A BuckMe Premium account opens in Chapter 3, with 20 percent off RydeMe among its perks (GamesRadar+).||

blocks.title: Loot needs a fence
blocks.text: Loot cannot be spent until a fence buys it or it is laundered, and drugs, jewelry and cars each go to a different fence (TGG). ||PowerPyx names seven fences, each paying its own rates, and says marked bills from banks and payday loan stores need a Dye Pack Jammer first. Robberies & Stealing covers them.||

blocks.title: What Wasted or Busted costs
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson told Famitsu that carried cash is at risk when you are Wasted or Busted. ||Launch guides agree that all pocket cash goes, with any loot bags, vehicles that were not yours and weapons picked up rather than bought; owned vehicles and weapons are kept (Game Rant, GamesRadar+). Push Square and IGN's beginner's guide say BuckMe money is safe, but IGN's Wanted guide says a small amount comes out of the checking account too. GamesRadar+ adds that aggressive civilians can take pocket cash.||

blocks.title: What money buys
blocks.text: Clothes, weapons, car upgrades, garages and registering stolen vehicles as your own, TGG reports, and at some points the story needs a set amount before it moves on. ||Launch sources back each of these: PowerPyx lists clothing stores, gun stores, mod shops and eight garages for sale, and TheSixthAxis's review says registering a car costs a fee that rises with its class.||

blocks.title: Spend early
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's money guide says saving up in Chapter 1 is pointless, because that money is lost when the chapter ends.||
Your criminal
A devil icon, sometimes with a halo, that tracks how each lead operates. TGG described it before launch from what Rob Nelson showed him; launch guides name the tiers and what moves them.

blocks.caption: A long-haired man aiming a pistol at a tattooed biker in the foreground.

blocks.title: The tiers
blocks.text: Before launch TGG reported four states: professional, aggressive, violent and psycho. ||PowerPyx and IGN list five, best to worst: Professional, Hardened, Violent, Psycho and Irredeemable. TheSixthAxis's review speaks of five while naming four of them, without Psycho, and DayOne's review describes four levels: professional, aggressive, psycho and irredeemable.||

blocks.title: Not the honor system
blocks.text: TGG asked whether it was Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system. Nelson said it is quite different: it describes how you operate as a criminal, not how good a person you are.

blocks.title: What moves it
blocks.text: Restraint and control move it up; shooting people you do not need to shoot moves it down. ||PowerPyx says Professional comes from stealth, harming no one in robberies, destroying tapes and disabling alarms; Hardened from putting enemies down without killing them; Violent from killing enemies, police or civilians; Psycho from killing sprees, killing domestic animals or driving over gravestones. IGN says mission choices move it too, GamesRadar+ that disabling police vehicles counts toward Hardened, and DayOne's review that your AI partner's kills do not count.||

blocks.title: One each, and where to see it
blocks.text: Jason and Lucia have separate profiles, shown on the HUD and in a menu tab with their relationship status. ||Open the map, tab with L1 (LB) to Jason & Lucia, then press Left or Right for each lead (IGN). The rating sits at the top of the lead's page (PowerPyx).||

blocks.caption: The Jason & Lucia tab, showing a criminal profile.

blocks.title: Hiding the notifications
blocks.text: The notifications can be switched off; your actions still count. ||PowerPyx says the switch is under Settings, UI, HUD Notifications, Criminal Profile.||

blocks.title: What it changes
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the profile has little direct effect, but it decides which actions raise Focus: stealth takedowns and non-lethal incapacitations at Professional and Hardened, headshots at Violent and Psycho, and nothing at Irredeemable. At Psycho and Irredeemable the police may shoot on sight and will not accept surrender (PowerPyx, IGN). GameSpot says a lead with a violent profile acts more violently when you are not controlling them.||

blocks.title: It can break
blocks.text: Pushed far enough, the icon cracks and then shatters, and as Nelson described it the bottom state can lock in for the rest of the playthrough. ||IGN says time slows and the Psycho icon cracks three times as a warning before it shatters to the grey Irredeemable icon. Irredeemable is permanent; only loading an earlier save undoes it (IGN, PowerPyx, TheSixthAxis). IGN says killing police mostly pushes toward Psycho, and blowing up civilian vehicles and crowds is the quickest way to Irredeemable.||

items: ||What the profile changes in the story, if anything. PowerPyx says it has little direct effect; TGG was told before launch there could be consequences.||

blocks.text: Jason and Lucia:
Time together builds a relationship between the two leads. Nelson and TGG described it before launch; launch guides name its four levels.

blocks.caption: Lucia leaning on the door of an open-top car, smiling, with Jason beside her holding a drink.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason and Lucia 03"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.title: Built by time together
blocks.text: The relationship grows when the pair spend time together: exploring, playing pool or mini golf, kayaking, or robbing places. IGN reports that the romance is optional, and Nelson says it gives no particular gameplay benefit: they stay partners in crime either way. TGG adds that dates are not booked as in earlier games, and relays IGN's interview that missions together are not enough to keep a romance going.

blocks.title: Four levels
blocks.text: TGG relayed Edge magazine's preview that closeness has four levels. ||IGN names them, lowest first: Running On Empty (a broken purple heart), Not So Hot (a half-broken heart), Crazy In Love (a pink heart) and Hot Together (a flaming heart). DayOne's review also counts four.||

blocks.caption: The Jason & Lucia tab with the relationship status.

blocks.title: Where to see it
blocks.text: ||At the bottom of the Jason & Lucia tab of the map screen, and on the heart between the two portraits in the quick menu opened by holding Right. A pink heart with a plus marks a gain, a purple broken heart with a minus a loss, and a flaming heart a big gain (IGN).||

blocks.title: What raises it
blocks.text: ||IGN lists invitations to hang out, hugs and kisses (L2 or LT, then Square or X at the heart prompt), talking while driving, dancing at clubs, holding hands (hold R2 or RT), handing over food or drink, exercising and committing crimes together. TheSixthAxis's review names robbing stores, working out, texting and eating out. GameSpot says a heart icon marks activities that count, and PowerPyx that meditating together counts twice. After a full day together, a heart around the home on the map suggests going back to rest (GamesRadar+).||

blocks.title: What lowers it
blocks.text: ||Ignoring calls, texts or greetings, long spells apart and driving off without your partner (IGN). TheSixthAxis's review names leaving your partner behind while running from the police, and GamesRadar+ ignoring their messages after a robbery. IGN says Hot Together needs both leads to put in the effort.||

blocks.caption: Lucia and Jason on a dock beside jet skis, with an on-screen prompt.

blocks.title: What it does not change
blocks.text: ||IGN says the pair can be intimate at the top two levels, with a cooldown of at least a couple of real-world hours, and that no other character can be romanced; GameSpot says these scenes are not interactive. Dying does not change the relationship (Game Rant), and it has no effect on trophies (PowerPyx).||

blocks.title: A head start in Chapter 1
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says optional Chapter 1 jobs done as Jason before Lucia is picked up give the couple a stronger start: fixing up the house and the Ganado, a haircut, a necklace, flowers, groceries and fetching Lucia's clothes from Andy. They vanish once she is picked up; doing them all should leave the pair at Crazy In Love.||

items: ||Whether the relationship changes how the story ends. No launch source read says so.||

blocks.text: Controls

Before launch only a few controls were known, from TGG watching the game being played. Launch guides and Rockstar's support pages fill in the rest. Buttons are given for PlayStation, with Xbox in brackets.

blocks.caption: The Controls settings screen, with an Xbox controller diagram labelled with the on-foot layout.

blocks.title: On foot
blocks.text: Sprint is a click of the left stick and cover is on R1. Crouching is back, you can strafe while crouched, and you can switch shoulders when aiming. TGG relayed another preview that the default walking speed can be changed, including to a jog. ||Push Square confirms that the Default scheme runs on L3, and puts jump on Cross (A).||

blocks.title: In a vehicle
blocks.text: The handbrake is X (A). L1 and R1 are used for shooting while driving, and filling up at a gas station is done by holding R2.

blocks.title: Three control schemes
blocks.text: ||Settings offers Default, Classic (in the style of Grand Theft Auto V) and Left-Handed, with a preview of each input on foot and in vehicles; IGN says none gives an advantage. Rockstar's settings article lists separate layouts for On Foot, Aiming, Melee, Land / Water Vehicles, Aircraft, Bicycle, Swimming and Parachute. Can I Play That? could not confirm that single buttons can be remapped.||

blocks.title: Aiming
blocks.text: ||TheSixthAxis's review says lock-on aiming is the default and that the settings allow free aim with aim assist switched off. Can I Play That? lists adjustable aim assist with separate toggles for drive-by and general shooting help, and DayOne's review says the aim dead zone can be set.||

blocks.title: First person, sometimes
blocks.text: ||There is no full first-person mode (TheSixthAxis). PowerPyx says holding L2 and pressing R3 while standing still gives a first-person view in which you cannot walk, and that driving with the phone out is in first person. A gun with an optic can be aimed in first person; iron sights cannot (PowerPyx, GameSpot).||

blocks.caption: A first-person view down a pistol with a red-dot sight inside a gun store, a purple bar at the top left.

blocks.title: Camera options
blocks.text: Kill cams and the crash camera can each be switched off, TGG reports. ||Rockstar's settings article lists Camera options for On Foot, Land & Water Vehicles, Comfort, Aircraft, Underwater and Cinematic.||

blocks.title: Photo mode
blocks.text: TGG saw a photo studio mode at the preview, and no director mode. ||Game Rant says it is opened from the pause menu, from the prologue on. It offers eight aspect ratios, field of view up to 48.5 degrees, depth of field and focus controls, colour and lens effects, 17 filters and up to five added lights, and the character can be hidden.||

blocks.caption: The Photo Studio screen, with a camera settings panel on the left and Jason in front of a city skyline.

blocks.text: Settings
There is no difficulty setting. Settings, opened from the pause menu, hold separate assists instead, along with the display and controller options.

blocks.caption: ||The settings categories in Rockstar Support's article. Restore All and Restore Default at the bottom of the screen undo changes.||
rows: ||Layouts for on foot, aiming, melee, land and water vehicles, aircraft, bicycle, swimming and parachute||
||Aim and look sensitivity, inverted controls, and DualSense features on PlayStation 5||
||Scaling and readability, subtitles and captions, navigation, reticle, combat, HUD and progress notifications, player and vehicle status, prompts, activities and units of measurement||
||On foot, land and water vehicles, comfort, aircraft, underwater and cinematic||

blocks.caption: The Settings menu with its category tabs across the top, open on the controls tab.

blocks.title: Two assists instead of difficulty
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and GameSpot say there are no difficulty levels. At the bottom of Settings, Gameplay, Push Square finds Accessible Combat, which lowers the damage you take in gunfights and raises the damage you deal, and Reduced Vehicle Damage, which protects your vehicle. The game warns that both change the balance of play; Push Square says they do not alter the story or switch off trophies. PC Gamer traced viral clips of planes bouncing off towers to Reduced Vehicle Damage.||

blocks.caption: The Gameplay tab with the Accessible Combat toggle highlighted and Reduced Vehicle Damage below it.

blocks.title: What the HUD shows
blocks.text: TGG reports a "classic" option that keeps the minimap on screen at all times, and a compass in its place. ||Can I Play That? lists both. PowerPyx says the minimap and the fuel gauge can be set to appear only when Down is pressed, that notifications for collectibles and the criminal profile are switched on under UI, HUD Notifications, and that brightness is under Display, Brightness Calibration.||

blocks.title: How it runs
blocks.text: Rockstar said before launch that the game targets 30 frames per second on both consoles, with PSSR upscaling and ray-traced shadows added on PlayStation 5 Pro. In a statement reported by VGC, Rockstar says PlayStation 5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X upscale from 1440p to 4K, and Xbox Series S from 720p to 1080p. Its technology production director told Kotaku the PS5 Pro's processor is not strong enough for a higher frame rate.

blocks.caption: Lucia firing a pistol from a convertible on a busy city street.
blocks.credit: Official screenshot, Rockstar Games, via VGC

blocks.text: Digital Foundry, as reported by Pure Xbox and VGC, ranks PlayStation 5 Pro the best version, finds small dips on the standard PlayStation 5 and calls Xbox Series S the least steady. Push Square's review on PS5 Pro found no 60 frames per second option.
Accessibility

Can I Play That? gathered the accessibility settings seen in reviews and live streams. It says Rockstar gave no review copies to accessibility outlets, so it had not played the game itself, and its list may be incomplete or wrong in places.

blocks.title: Play and controls
blocks.text: ||A toggle that lowers enemy health and the damage you and your vehicle take; simplified minigames; five levels of tap assist for quick-time events; holds that can become toggles, with a delay against accidental presses; three controller presets; and adjustable stick and trigger sensitivity and haptics. DayOne's review says button-mashing prompts can become holds.||

blocks.title: Letting the car drive
blocks.text: ||With a destination set, hold Down on the D-pad and press Options (Menu) for the cinematic camera, then hold Circle (B) and the vehicle drives itself; the triggers change its speed (IGN, Game Rant). It mostly keeps to the road rules and works in boats along navigable water. DayOne's review says it works well once a destination is set, but it crashed in aircraft and struggled to find a path on narrow waterways.||

blocks.caption: A car driving itself in the cinematic camera.

blocks.title: Sound
blocks.text: TGG reported a streamer mode that turns off copyrighted music. ||Can I Play That? lists subtitles and captions that can be resized, with an optional background and speaker names; a toggle that removes the ringing after explosions; mono audio; and separate volume sliders for effects, interface, dialogue, music and media.||

blocks.title: Sight
blocks.text: ||Narration for most menus and a screen reader from the first start, with a separate audio description toggle; a high contrast mode and a colourblind option that strengthens the Focus trail colours; adjustable text size, interface colours, objective marker size and map icon size; and an adjustable reticle. Rockstar's own settings list confirms High-Contrast Shaders under Display and a Scaling & Readability group under UI.||

blocks.title: Comfort and content
blocks.text: ||Settings for motion blur, head bob, camera movement and screen effects; reduced flashbang intensity; and adjustable blood and gore, with dismemberment able to be switched off. Rockstar's settings list has a Comfort group under Camera.||

items: ||Whether single buttons can be remapped. Can I Play That? could not confirm it and thinks it is probably missing.||

blocks.text: Saving and
How the game keeps your progress, and what happens when a lead is Wasted or Busted. Little was published before launch; launch guides now agree on most of it.

blocks.title: Fifteen slots and an autosave
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx, GamesRadar+ and GameSpot all give 15 manual save slots. PowerPyx and GamesRadar+ count the autosave as a sixteenth, while GameSpot says it takes one of the fifteen. Notebookcheck says autosaves do not show in the Save Game menu and are loaded from the separate Load Game screen.||

blocks.caption: The pause menu with Game selected, above Store, Help, Photo Studio and Settings.

blocks.title: Saving by hand
blocks.text: ||Open the pause menu and choose Game, then Save Game, anywhere in free roam. It is usually greyed out during missions (PowerPyx), and DayOne's review says it is also unavailable in combat.||

blocks.title: When the autosave runs
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says after missions, when Wasted or Busted, and after major open-world encounters. In Kotaku's testing it ran after main missions and larger side missions, but not after small optional jobs and never during a mission. PowerPyx says loading an older manual save overwrites the autosave too.||

blocks.title: Crashes and quitting
blocks.text: ||Kotaku and Notebookcheck report players losing hours of progress after crashes or switching the console off; Rockstar had not commented when they were read. DayOne's review says resuming through the console's Quick Resume caused visual glitches that saving and reloading fixed. TheSixthAxis's review says a weapon picked up in the world is lost when you quit unless it has been stored.||

blocks.title: Save before you quit
blocks.text: ||Kotaku recommends pausing, saving by hand and only then quitting.||

blocks.title: Keep a save for each chapter
blocks.text: ||Missions cannot be replayed, though free roam carries on after the story (PowerPyx). All three save guides advise keeping a save at the start and end of each of the five chapters, and GameSpot adds that earlier homes can only be visited again this way.||

blocks.title: Cheats switch saving off
blocks.text: ||Cheats unlock after the story, and using any of them switches saving off; GamesRadar+ says you must then quit and reload a save. The Encyclopedia lists the cheats.||

blocks.title: Wasted and Busted
blocks.text: Nelson said that if either lead is arrested it is Busted and a restart, as in earlier games. ||Game Rant says a lead who dies comes back nearby, and that neither the relationship nor the criminal profile changes. The autosave runs, and a personal vehicle you were driving is impounded (GamesRadar+). Buffs from food, sleep and showers end. No guide read gives a hospital bill or a fine. What it costs in money is on the Cash, Bank & Loot page.||

chapters.title: Story & Missions
chapters.intro: How the story is laid out, how missions work and who hands out the work. No plot: missions are described by who gives them, where they start and what they pay or unlock. Almost everything here comes from the released game, so it stays covered until you choose to see spoilers.

blocks.text: The story's
Before launch, previews said only that the story comes in chapters. Launch guides now give the layout: how many chapters, who you play in each, and where the pair live.

blocks.title: Chapters
blocks.text: TGG's preview report said the story is divided into chapters. ||PowerPyx's walkthrough lists a prologue and five chapters. The trophy list has a trophy for finishing each of Chapters 1 to 4 and one for the final mission.||

blocks.title: How many missions
blocks.text: ||Counting the walkthrough's entries that are not marked optional gives 25, 18, 31, 34 and 10 for the five chapters. Some are short errands, and GTABase numbers its story list differently, so there is no agreed total.||

blocks.title: Who you play, and when
blocks.frameAlt: A woman in a dark jacket stands in a wood-panelled motel room with a television and dresser
blocks.text: ||The prologue is played as Lucia. Most of Chapter 1 is played as Jason, with Lucia taking the last two missions. Lucia becomes playable in the open world at the start of Chapter 2, and free switching between the two opens with the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break. GameSpot puts that point at roughly 30 percent of the story.||

blocks.title: A home for each chapter
blocks.frameAlt: A man walks along a palm-lined Vice City street past neon-lit Art Deco buildings at dusk
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says each chapter is built around a different safehouse, and that new activities open up as the home changes. The table below gives the homes the guides name.||

blocks.title: How long it takes
blocks.text: TGG says Rob Nelson's most recent playthrough took about 80 hours, with the story and some optional content. ||PowerPyx's trophy guide estimates 60 to 80 hours for the story with its optional missions, and about 200 hours for everything.||

blocks.caption: The chapters at a glance

blocks.text: Moving between
A chapter ends at a fixed mission, and some things do not come with you. Guides call these points of no return. This page covers what closes, what happens to money, and what each chapter opens.

blocks.caption: People stand outside a red-lit club entrance on a city street at night

blocks.title: The old home stays behind
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says an earlier safehouse cannot be revisited without loading an older save. GTABase says starting the last Chapter 2 mission means losing the Starlet Motel as a home for good.||

blocks.title: Leaving Chapter 1
blocks.frameAlt: Jason using a cash machine outside a building
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx marks Recalibration as the Chapter 1 point of no return: Chapter 1 free roam ends, and pocket cash carried into the following missions is lost. Its money guide says saving up in Chapter 1 is pointless for that reason. IGN suggests finishing leftover Key Lento tasks before Tourist Trap.||

blocks.title: Leaving Chapter 2
blocks.frameAlt: A map screenshot from IGN's Checking Out walkthrough
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says Checking Out, the last Chapter 2 mission, needs every other Chapter 2 main mission done and at least $15,000, and that starting it ends the chapter. IGN says having $15,000 in the BuckMe checking account makes it unlock sooner.||

blocks.title: Bank limits follow the story
blocks.text: ||Rockstar Support says BuckMe account limits rise only as the main story moves on, and that payments held up by a full account go through once it is upgraded. PowerPyx says the Premium tier is given at the start of Chapter 4, and that the Chapter 4 mission Another Life brings the Black account with a $2,000,000 limit. Money put into Family Savings cannot be taken out again, but raises the checking limit; DayOne's review says each chapter's savings target is rewarded.||

blocks.title: Heists close a chapter
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says The Cartel Heist needs every other Chapter 3 main mission done, and its money guide says the story pays $120,000 at the end of that chapter. The walkthrough groups the Chapter 4 preparation jobs under one finale in the same way.||

blocks.title: Before Recalibration
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx advises keeping a separate manual save and putting at least $5,000 into Family Savings before starting it, since pocket cash is lost afterwards.||

blocks.caption: What the story opens, chapter by chapter (PowerPyx, GTABase and PC Gamer)
steps: ||Chapter 1: Just a Scratch opens mod shops and Pay 'n' Spray; Buck Me opens the bank app.||
||Chapter 2: Moses gives the Slim Jim and the Scooter Bros app; Daily Driver opens garage buying; Coffee Break opens free switching.||
||Chapter 3: Credit Check marks banks and payday loan stores as targets; Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS gives the Key Cloner; the Jack of Hearts club opens after a story mission.||
||Chapter 4: after VCIA Takedown, Yasmani's optional That's Where The Money Is... opens bank vault robberies.||
||After the story: the map stays open apart from a few mission-only buildings, and cheats appear in the Progress menu.||

items: ||Whether pocket cash is lost at the later chapter breaks. The guides read mention it only for Chapter 1.||
||Where the pair live in Chapter 5.||

blocks.text: Reading the
Missions are picked from the map, not from a list. Launch guides describe how the markers are coloured and lettered, and what to do when one will not start.

blocks.caption: The in-game map of Leonard and Kelly County with the Deliver Packages mission card open

blocks.title: Three colours
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide says mandatory story missions have pink icons with black letters, optional missions black icons with pink letters, and side tasks are purple.||

blocks.title: J and L
blocks.frameAlt: A map screenshot from IGN's Gone Fishing walkthrough, near the start of the mission
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a J or L on a mission's map icon means it must be played by that character alone, and a darkened portrait means the partner is busy for now. PowerPyx says the other lead may be greyed out while you are at home.||

blocks.title: Two names for one mission
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx explains that a mission's label on the map differs from the title shown once it starts. Tourist Trap shows on the map as Take Up Mattia's Offer, and Checking Out as Move to Vice City.||

blocks.title: Initials for the people who give work
blocks.text: ||Some regular contacts have their own green icon with their initials. PowerPyx names a green KR for Kenton Rees's jobs in Key Lento and a green RK for Randy in the west of Vice City.||

blocks.title: Hourglass and lock
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says a mission with an hourglass icon is open for a limited time and should be done as soon as it appears, or it is missed. GTABase says a marker showing a lock means the person is not available yet; for one of Yago's missions, sleeping and coming back in the afternoon or evening fixes it.||

blocks.title: Smaller marks inside a job
blocks.frameAlt: A map screenshot of where Shirley's rum errand begins in Key Lento
blocks.text: ||Errands put their own purple marks on the map: Push Square describes a purple bottle for Shirley's rum, and PowerPyx says Bret Vogel marks hunting spots and Yasmani's tips mark security vans in purple. Eurogamer and Push Square say the optional repairs at Jason's house carry small paintbrush icons.||

blocks.title: Missions without a marker
blocks.text: ||A few start another way. PowerPyx says Save for the Future has no map marker and runs from the BuckMe app. PC Gamer says Dubious Provenance starts from an icon on an object in the Bayside apartment, and PowerPyx says Pool Day starts by talking to Lucia on the hotel balcony.||
Mission
What Rockstar said about failing, and what launch guides found about replays, difficulty and saving.

blocks.caption: Lucia and Nicole working the vault door

blocks.title: Built to fail you less
blocks.text: Rockstar's vice president of technology, David Hynd, told GamesRadar+ the team wanted fewer mission fails for players who experiment, and used more of the game's regular systems and AI inside missions. Stephen Donkin, vice president of design, said they worked to blur the line between on-mission and off-mission play. ||GamesRadar+'s reviewer says checkpoints are better than in Grand Theft Auto V and Red Dead Redemption 2, with a Retry Checkpoint option.||

blocks.title: No replay
blocks.frameAlt: Jason aiming a pistol in an alley
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says there is no mission replay and no chapter select: neither story missions nor Strangers & Freaks missions can be played again. Dexerto words it differently: a mission can be replayed only by loading an older manual save, since no mission can be picked from a menu.||

blocks.title: No medals, no difficulty
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says missions have no gold medals; the only medals are for shooting range and race challenges. PowerPyx and GameSpot say there are no difficulty levels. Push Square describes two toggles under Settings, Gameplay: Accessible Combat and Reduced Vehicle Damage. It says they do not change the story or switch off trophies.||

blocks.title: Saving around missions
blocks.text: ||There are 15 manual save slots and an autosave. PowerPyx says manual saving is usually greyed out during missions; GamesRadar+ says the game autosaves after missions. All three guides read advise keeping a save at the start and end of each of the five chapters, because missions cannot be replayed.||

blocks.title: Wasted or Busted
blocks.text: If either lead is arrested it is "Busted" and a restart, Rob Nelson told IGN before launch. ||Launch guides add that being Wasted or Busted costs all pocket cash and any loot bags carried, while owned weapons and vehicles are kept, and that it triggers an autosave.||

blocks.title: What can be missed
blocks.frameAlt: Jason running past a car in a parking garage
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says nothing counted by the 100% checklist can be missed. Some optional missions and items do close as the story moves on, though: Shirley's errands go once Tourist Trap starts, and Bad Driver is gone once Power Play is done. The Optional Work page lists more.||

blocks.title: If a mission breaks
blocks.text: ||GTABase reports a bug in Checking Out: dying during the motorbike chase can leave no objective and a police search area that cannot be escaped. It advises restarting the mission if that happens.||
Choices inside

Previews said choices can change later events. Launch guides describe the choices you meet in practice: how well a job goes, what you pick up, and a few clear either-or moments. What is chosen in story terms is left out here.

blocks.title: What previews said
blocks.text: TGG reports that choices you make can affect later events. He relays IGN's preview that the tower-block escape in the Extended Look has more than one route out, and that another mission suggests an escape route without forcing it.

blocks.title: How well it goes
blocks.frameAlt: The compound where the Canis Crawler is parked in Daily Driver
blocks.text: ||Many payouts move with your performance. IGN gives Gone Fishing as $100 to $220 depending on how well it goes. Daily Driver adds $500 and Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS adds $10,000 if the car arrives in good condition. Pilot Pete's delivery runs pay $20,000 only if every package arrives in time.||

blocks.title: Preparation carries forward
blocks.frameAlt: A small plane parked on an overgrown airstrip
blocks.text: ||Set-up jobs feed the big one. PowerPyx says how Company Property goes decides how many explosives are available in Hidden Charges, and the number of bombs placed there sets how much time The Cartel Heist allows.||

blocks.title: Things to pick up on the way
blocks.text: ||Some missions hide optional pickups that cannot be collected later. PowerPyx notes a cash pickup in Gone Fishing that raises the Professional rating; others are the Macizo Cigar in Pipework, the unique pistols in Don Gone and The Missing Link, and Andy's Jacket in Home Sweet Home.||

blocks.title: Either-or moments
blocks.frameAlt: A light blue car driving down a small-town street
blocks.text: ||A few missions end on a choice that changes the reward. Bad Driver pays $20,000 one way and leads to a follow-up mission that hands over a car the other. Kyle's last mission pays $5,000 or nothing, and Kirk's last can add $10,000. One outcome of Eddie Acosta's party costs $50,000. PC Gamer says the choice in Dubious Provenance makes little difference: one way pays a watch up front, the other only delays the mission.||

blocks.title: Small choices
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia at the doorway of the antique store
blocks.text: ||Not every choice matters. Eurogamer says the wrong answers to a crossword clue in the prologue only change the dialogue. IGN says Coffee Break is where you pick which of three optional jobs Lucia does first.||

blocks.title: Choices and your record
blocks.text: ||IGN says mission choices also move the criminal profile. A secret trophy, Actions Speak Louder, is described only as "Choices made (for better or worse)".||

items: ||Whether choices change later missions or the ending. The launch sources read do not say.||

blocks.text: Optional work and
Beside the main missions sit optional story missions and the Strangers & Freaks side lines. This page covers who offers them and how they begin; the next two pages list the people.

blocks.title: Optional story missions
blocks.frameAlt: Jason at the fruit and vegetable shelves inside a grocery store
blocks.text: ||In Chapter 1, Lucia asks Jason for small errands, such as groceries, flowers or a haircut, that raise their relationship. Cal adds optional jobs at the Rusty Anchor and a fishing challenge. Chapter 2 has a pawn shop and a bowling alley to rob, and Chapter 4 has Yasmani's That's Where The Money Is..., which opens bank vaults.||

blocks.title: Strangers & Freaks
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 14 strangers with 39 missions between them, first available from Chapter 1 to Chapter 4. A trophy asks for eight strands to be finished. Kenton Rees has a trophy of his own but is not in that list, so it may be incomplete.||

blocks.title: Met in person or by flyer
blocks.frameAlt: Searching the swamp at night with a flashlight
blocks.text: ||Shirley calls out to Jason near his house. Kirk's Skunk Ape flyers hang in shop windows; reading one saves his number, and his first job can only be played at night. Kyle's first job is marked by a flyer next to the Starlet Motel office.||

blocks.title: By call or text
blocks.text: ||Andy phones Lucia in Chapter 3. Pilot Pete phones Jason early in Chapter 4, shortly after Pool Day. Bret Vogel texts Jason some time after Coffee Break, and Manuel texts about Yago's first street race. Eddie Acosta, met at the hotel pool, texts an invitation a few days later.||

blocks.title: Marked for you
blocks.text: ||Some strands appear on the map by themselves. PowerPyx says Billy's first race is marked after Coffee Break, Randy's wish list after Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, and Tyrone's Spin On This once enough Kitty Litter Labs are destroyed.||

blocks.title: Who can take them
blocks.text: ||Most can be played as either lead. Andy's are for Lucia only and Pilot Pete's for Jason only. Kirk's last mission needs Lucia at night, so it cannot be done before Chapter 2. Billy's Mall Rats and Eddie Acosta's party need one lead on their own, not the pair.||

blocks.title: Windows that close, and ones that stay open
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says Shirley's errands close when Tourist Trap starts; Push Square says at the start of Chapter 2. Bad Driver closes once Power Play is done, and Race Against Yago is a limited-time mission. Bret Vogel's hunting, Randy's wish list and Tyrone's labs stay available after the story.||

blocks.text: What Rockstar showed

blocks.caption: The six places Rockstar named before launch
rows: The crowded heart of Leonida: pastel hotels and white sand at Ocean Beach, the bakeries of Little Cuba, the Tisha-Wocka flea market and VC Port.
The island chain south of Vice City. Smuggling country, and where Jason's story starts.
Swamp, mangroves and shallow water between the city and the interior, famous for its alligators.
A former holiday town of cheap motels, shut attractions and empty strip malls.
Inland sugar country around the Allied Crystal refinery, with a local biker gang.
Forest and high ground at the top of the map, pitched for hunting, fishing and off-road trails.

blocks.text: The five counties on the released map

||PowerPyx's map guide lists five counties, and Rockstar's six places sit inside them: the Keys and Grassrivers in Mariana County, Vice City in Vice-Dale County, Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia in Kelly County, and Mount Kalaga in Lummox County.||

blocks.title: Mariana County, the south
blocks.text: ||The Keys from Mile Zero Air Station and Southwind to Key Lento, the swamps of Pelican Valley, Grassrivers, Watson Bay and Capri.||

blocks.title: Vice-Dale County, the city
blocks.text: ||Vice City itself, Vice Beach across the bay with Ocean Beach and Washington Beach, the town of Hamlet to the south and the airport area, VCIA, on the west side.||

blocks.title: Kelly County, the north-west
blocks.text: ||Port Gellhorn, Draper Island, Buckskin Swamp and the farmland and canyons of North Kelly County. PowerPyx's store lists and GTABase put Ambrosia here too, although Ambrosia is missing from PowerPyx's list of map regions.||

blocks.caption: A rainy Belville street with a gas station, inside a phone video frame from Trailer 1.

blocks.title: Leonard County, the north-east
blocks.text: ||Belville, the shops and mall of Waning Sands, and Lake Leonida with Richard Barebone State Park in the north.||

blocks.title: Lummox County, the north
blocks.text: ||Mount Kalaga National Park, the towns of Grayson and Millport, Bonanza with the MacAlister Gold Mine, and the Kalaga Reservoir behind Dawson Dam.||

blocks.caption: Two characters at the rocky Kalaga Lookout, high above forested hills.

items: ||Some places are filed under different areas on different PowerPyx pages: Hamlet under Vice-Dale or Mariana County, Buckskin Swamp under Kelly or Vice-Dale County, and Leaf Links under Vice City or Vice Beach.||

blocks.text: Vice City:
blocks.sub: Leonida's biggest city, district by district

blocks.text: Vice City is the series' stand-in for Miami and its first return there since 2002. Rockstar named only a handful of districts before launch; launch guides have mapped the rest.

blocks.caption: The hazy, sunlit Downtown Vice City skyline with the tall Piker tower in the middle, a helicopter and a Ferris wheel at the edge.

blocks.title: Named before launch
blocks.text: Rockstar's material names Ocean Beach with its pastel art deco hotels, Little Cuba and its bakeries, the Tisha-Wocka flea market, VC Port (billed as the cruise ship capital of the world), La Perle, Stockyard, Tequesta and Vice Beach.

blocks.title: Downtown and the towers
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's map puts Downtown at the centre, with large Lombank and Fleeca vaults, the Downtown and Downtown North train stations and the Dock Ring. GTABase's map lists the Piker Financial Center, the Palaestra Tower and the Galina Ballet Opera House along Catalan Boulevard, in Downtown and Bayside.||

blocks.title: The inland districts
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx also lists Little Cuba, La Perle, Salton, Rockridge, Crosstown, Bayside, Balsero, Southside, Peacock Bay, Tequesta, Tequesta Retreat, Stockyard and the Decor District. Stockyard has the murals GTABase compares to Miami's Wynwood, and the Decor District is where the fashion stores cluster.||

blocks.caption: A Vice City street under an overpass whose pillars are painted with large murals, with a blue sedan and dirt bikes on the road.

blocks.title: Vice Beach
blocks.text: ||Across the bay, Vice Beach is Ocean Beach and Washington Beach on the Atlantic side. PowerPyx counts 60 bars in Ocean Beach alone, and GTABase's map puts the Ocean View Hotel from GTA Vice City back on Shore Drive. Washington Beach holds three of the sculptures the WAiNK app can scan.||

blocks.caption: Shore Drive at night after rain: the neon-lit hotel row behind palms, with a sports car and parked scooters in front.

blocks.title: The islands
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's list includes the Rialto Islands, Starfish Island, Waxman Island, Catalan Key, Gloriana Key, Port Vice City and Dalton Island. Dalton Island cannot be reached by taxi: take the ferry from Waxman Island, a boat or an aircraft.||

items: Rockstar has not published a district list of its own. The names on this page come from the in-game map as launch guides read it.

blocks.text: Getting around:
blocks.sub: Uncovering the map, taxis, trains and landmarks

blocks.text: How the map fills in, how to cross it without driving, and the landmarks launch guides point to.

blocks.title: Uncovering the map
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says shops appear on the map only once the fog over their area is cleared, and each filtered list counts what you have found. Its aircraft guide suggests a plane from the Key Lento airstrip near Jason's house for uncovering the map, because its fuel lasts. GamesRadar+ says the map index has nine tabs, and holding Down on the D-pad shows nearby shops and missions in the world.||

blocks.title: Taxis instead of fast travel
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide says there is no fast travel from the map. Paradise Taxi, a phone contact from the end of the first mission, takes you to any marker, even one you have not visited, and $100 on top of the fare skips the ride. The RydeMe app arrives in Chapter 2 and charges by distance; skipping costs $100 there too. GTABase says taxis cannot reach isolated spots such as the remote keys or deep swamp.||

blocks.caption: The in-game phone with the taxi contact circled in the contacts list, held in front of an orange taxi.

blocks.title: Trains, buses and the ferry
blocks.text: ||Buses and trains run to a timetable: wait at the stop, choose a destination once aboard and hold Triangle (Y on Xbox) to skip the journey. PowerPyx counts 25 train stations, 17 of them in Vice-Dale County, and GameSpot says a line runs the length of Leonida. The only ferry links Waxman Island and Dalton Island for $50.||

blocks.caption: The in-game map of southern Leonida with the train station list open and the first station marked.

blocks.title: Airports and restricted ground
blocks.text: ||Vice City International Airport sits on the west side of Vice-Dale County; GameSpot says crossing its restricted gate brings three stars. Mile Zero Air Station, on Goose Key at the south-west end of the Keys, keeps fighter jets and tanks, and PowerPyx says taking a jet brings four stars. Aircraft are covered in the Vehicles chapter.||

blocks.title: Landmarks worth a look
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 31 landmarks and 23 sculptures that the WAiNK phone app can scan, among them the Dock Ring Downtown, the Gellhorn Fun Fair, Belpoint Lighthouse, the Lawton Co. Paper Mill at Moreau and the Pixel Fountain in Tequesta. The last meditation spot, Ascent Mountain, is at the peak of Mount Kalaga and appears only after the others are done.||

blocks.caption: A character looking up at the Dock Ring observation wheel past a palm tree.

blocks.title: The edge of the map
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says an aircraft that reaches the edge of the map runs out of fuel and crashes, and a jet ski heading out to sea runs dry and leaves the rider stranded.||

chapters.title: Characters
chapters.intro: The two leads and the supporting characters named in Rockstar's material, followed by the other people in the Encyclopedia whose entries are not spoilers.

blocks.text: Two leads:
blocks.sub: Who they are, as Rockstar introduces them

blocks.text: You play both. Getting Started covers switching and the relationship in detail; this page is about who the two are.

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia riding a green and purple Seashark jet ski at speed, with city towers behind.

blocks.title: Lucia Caminos
blocks.text: Lucia learned to fight from her father and has fought for her family ever since. That loyalty put her inside Leonida Penitentiary, and luck got her out. She wants the good life her mother has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City, and teaming up with Jason looks like her way to it.

blocks.title: Jason Duval
blocks.text: Jason grew up around small-time crooks. A spell in the Army was meant to straighten him out; instead he ended up in the Keys, working for local drug runners. He wants an easy life, and things keep getting harder.

blocks.title: Who plays them
blocks.text: Rockstar's official credits, published on November 19, list Dylan Rourke as Jason Duval and Manni L. Perez as Lucia Caminos.

blocks.title: Switching
blocks.text: Before launch Rob Nelson said switching was kept as open as possible, and that the lead you are not playing keeps a routine of their own. ||PowerPyx says free switching begins after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, with only Jason playable for most of Chapter 1. Holding Right on the D-pad opens the partner options.||

blocks.caption: Jason standing in the driveway of the green stilt house in Key Lento at sunset.

blocks.title: The relationship
blocks.text: Their relationship rises and falls with time spent together, and the romance is optional: they stay partners in crime either way. ||IGN names four levels, from Running On Empty to Hot Together. Hanging out, holding hands, dancing at clubs and working out together raise it; ignoring messages and driving off without your partner lower it.||

blocks.title: A head start for the couple
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says the optional Chapter 1 jobs Jason can do before Lucia's release, such as repairing his house, buying flowers and filling the fridge, give the pair a stronger start. They vanish once Lucia is picked up.||
The cast:
blocks.sub: From Rockstar's published bios

blocks.text: Rockstar's character pages introduced six supporting characters before launch. What part each plays in the story is left to the game.

blocks.title: Cal Hampton
blocks.text: Jason's friend and another of Brian Heder's associates. Happily paranoid, he spends his time at home with a few beers and the Coast Guard radio turned up. Jason has bigger plans; Cal would rather stay exactly where he is.

blocks.title: Brian Heder
blocks.text: An old-school drug runner from the golden age of Keys smuggling, still moving product through the boat yard he keeps with his third wife, Lori. He lets Jason stay rent-free at one of his properties in return for help with local shakedowns.
blocks.frameAlt: Brian Heder holding a clipboard and pointing, talking to someone in the foreground

blocks.title: Boobie Ike
blocks.text: A Vice City legend who turned street reputation into real estate, a strip club and a recording studio. What he cares about most is Only Raw Records, the label he runs with Dre'Quan Priest. All it needs now is a hit.

blocks.title: Dre'Quan Priest
blocks.text: More hustler than gangster: dealing paid the bills, but music was always the plan. He books the acts at Boobie's club, and signing Real Dimez could be the break that takes him further.
blocks.frameAlt: Two men standing at a mixing desk in a recording studio

blocks.title: Real Dimez
blocks.text: Bae-Luxe and Roxy, friends since school, who turned squeezing local dealers into rap tracks and a nonstop social feed. An early hit with the local rapper DWNPLY lifted them; five years later they are signed to Only Raw Records and chasing a second.

blocks.title: Raul Bautista
blocks.text: A veteran bank robber with the confidence, charm and patience of long practice, always recruiting people willing to take big risks. His recklessness raises the stakes with every score.

Rockstar's credits confirm Stephen Root as Brian Heder and name Bobby Moynihan as Cal, Mike Forbs as Boobie Ike, Naiqui Macabroad as Dre'Quan, Hood Brat as Bae-Luxe, Krissy Celess as Roxy Rashad and Manny Perez as Raul Bautista.
Met after launch

||Launch guides list many more people. Among them are Donnie, a seaplane pilot in Brian's circle who buys stolen goods in Key Lento early on; Tyrone, a fence in La Perle; Kat, a friend of the couple; and Valentina, Andrés de León and Petra Navarro, who are tied to the Megamundo company. Others include buyers for stolen goods and cars in Port Gellhorn and Vice City, a treasure hunter in Key Lento, a dirt bike crew and an old army friend of Jason's who runs a hunting business. PowerPyx lists 14 strangers with side missions of their own.||

blocks.caption: A character met after launch, in a frame from Rockstar's own footage.
