chapters.title: Vehicles
chapters.intro: Vehicles and vehicle types seen in Rockstar's material before launch, with names only where Rockstar published them, followed by the other vehicles in the Encyclopedia whose entries are not spoilers.

blocks.text: Vehicles:
blocks.sub: How the game sorts what you drive

blocks.text: Rockstar showed cars, bikes, boats and aircraft of every kind before launch. The released game keeps a record of every model you find.

Official images show muscle cars and sports cars in the city, airboats in Grassrivers, dirt bikes and an ATV in the mud at Mount Kalaga, jet skis and party boats in the Keys, and seaplanes and helicopters overhead.

blocks.caption: A business jet seen from below, banking against a pink evening sky.
||Base models in the Progress database, by class. PowerPyx and IGN give the same counts; IGN splits the service vehicles further.||
rows: ||47: 11 trucks, 9 utility, 8 military, 7 emergency, 6 industrial and 6 transport, per IGN||

blocks.title: 557 vehicles in all
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 557 vehicles in the Progress database: 277 base models and 280 Standout versions. IGN counts 277 regular vehicles and 281 standouts. Scanning a vehicle with the WAiNK phone app records it, and the 100% checklist asks for 200 base models.||

blocks.title: Standout vehicles
blocks.text: ||Standouts are one-off versions waiting in fixed places, and they do not count toward the 200 base models. PowerPyx sorts them into 25 groups (its database page says 26), from 5 Donks and 5 Lowriders to 20 Retro, 19 Ultra-Luxe and 30 Leonida Man; IGN's counts match except Street Racers, 17 against 16. Finding all 16 Girlypop vehicles unlocks the Neon Jungle screen filter.||

blocks.caption: A Willard Faction Custom Donk, in a frame from Rockstar's pre-launch trailers and screenshots.

blocks.title: Ultimate Edition and bonus vehicles
blocks.text: Rockstar lists the '95 Grotti Cheetah, the Vapid Ganado Retro Build, the '67 Vapid Dominator Buggy, the Shitzu Squalo boat and, for Jason's safehouse, a Dinka Enduro motorcycle and a Crest kayak in the Ultimate Edition. The Vintage Vice City Pack adds a '55 Vapid Stanier and a garage by Ocean Beach. ||Eurogamer, citing IGN, says the Enduro and the kayak can only be used during Chapter 1.||

blocks.title: Spawning vehicles with cheats
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 21 vehicles that can be spawned with cheats once the story is finished, each with its own unlock condition; the Lapwing Mallard seaplane, for example, needs five Vehicle challenges. Using a cheat switches off trophies and saving.||
Keeping a car:
blocks.sub: Personal vehicles, fees, garages and delivery

blocks.text: Before launch Rob Nelson told TGG that a stolen car can be registered as your own and kept in a garage, and that a phone app brings it to you. Launch guides fill in the costs.

blocks.title: Your personal vehicle
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says Jason and Lucia each have one personal vehicle at a time, always shown in the Personal tab of the map index, and that its trunk holds the loadout, outfits, stash bags and hunting spoils. PowerPyx says only Jason's own car is kept in Chapter 1.||

blocks.title: Registering a stolen car
blocks.text: ||Registration opens with the Chapter 2 mission Moses, at his garage in Port Gellhorn, for cars without a tracker. From early in Chapter 3 any Pay 'n' Spray registers cars with a standard tracker by swapping the plates. The fee follows the car's value: GameSpot says Moses discounts the first one and later fees can reach tens of thousands of dollars. A car with a standard tracker cannot be modified until it is registered.||

blocks.caption: ||Registration cost and stolen sell value of some common cars, from GTABase's database||

blocks.text: ||In these figures the stolen sell value is about 30 percent of the registration cost for cars with no tracker or a standard one, and about half for cars with an advanced tracker.||

blocks.title: Who buys stolen cars
blocks.text: ||Moses buys cars with no tracker, Pay 'n' Sprays take cars with a standard tracker from Chapter 3, and a buyer in Vice City wants certain high-end cars with advanced trackers once the Key Cloner is unlocked. Prices and the wish list are in the Money chapter.||

blocks.title: Garages
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 12 garages: eight with one parking spot each, sold through the Vice City Real Estate phone app from late in Chapter 2 for $4,000 to $40,000 ($160,000 in all), and four given by the story with up to three spots. It counts 18 vehicle slots at most, 16 in garages plus the two personal vehicles. GameSpot counts 10 garages and says none is in Lummox County. How many slots you start with is disputed: one (PowerPyx), three (GTABase) or four (GameSpot).||

blocks.caption: The in-game map zoomed in with the Mitchell Auto Center garage card open, showing one empty parking spot.

blocks.title: Delivery and the impound
blocks.text: ||The Scooter Bros app, from the Chapter 2 mission Moses, delivers any registered vehicle for a fee and recovers destroyed ones; Premium, $12,500 in the app, gives three free deliveries a day. Police impound a personal vehicle abandoned in a chase or driven when you are Wasted or Busted, and stash bags in its trunk may be lost. IGN says climbing the impound lot's fence and breaking out through the gate costs nothing.||

blocks.caption: A tow truck, in a frame from Rockstar's pre-launch trailers and screenshots.

blocks.title: Pay 'n' Sprays and mod shops
blocks.text: ||The 19 Pay 'n' Sprays repair, repaint, register and buy vehicles, and a colour change stops the police recognising the car. PowerPyx lists 14 mod shops, each with a speciality, from lowriders, hot rods and wraps to dirt bikes and choppers; two of them are Ultimate Edition only.||
blocks.frameAlt: A yellow car raised on stands in a garage, with one person underneath and another standing beside it

blocks.text: On the water:
blocks.sub: Where to find boats and aircraft, and which you can keep

blocks.text: Leonida lives on the water, and official images show seaplanes over the Keys and helicopters over everything. ||Launch guides say boats and aircraft are not kept the way cars are.||

blocks.title: Boats cannot be registered
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says no boat can be registered as Jason's or Lucia's personal vehicle, however it was obtained. A stolen boat can be left at a dock, though story progress seems to clear unowned vehicles away.||

blocks.title: The boats you start with
blocks.text: Rockstar pitches the Ultimate Edition's Shitzu Squalo for fishing in Gambit Bay. ||GameSpot says a fishing boat waits at the dock behind Jason's Key Lento house in every edition but cannot be recovered once the story leaves Key Lento, and that the custom Squalo is docked on Washington Island near the Y Hotel from just after Chapter 4 begins.||

blocks.title: Yachts and speedboats
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says yachts and luxury speedboats need the Key Cloner, which arrives in Chapter 4, while smaller and older boats can be hotwired. It points to unguarded yachts at the Leaf Links country club and the marinas of Ocean Beach and Washington Beach.||

blocks.caption: A dark-hulled motor yacht moored at a wooden dock with people on deck.

blocks.title: Planes you can take
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists planes at the Key Lento airstrip near Jason's house, west of the Mariana County swamps, south of Port Gellhorn and in central and north Kelly County. PC Gamer says the nearest to Jason's house are Mammoth Dodo seaplanes about 2.5 miles south-west along Route 1 in Southwind, with a Maverick helicopter on the dock, none of them guarded. Small two-seat planes at Wild Hog Point, west of Port Gellhorn, did not bring the police for GameSpot.||

blocks.caption: A white and yellow Mammoth Dodo seaplane flying over blue water.

blocks.title: Helicopters
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists helicopters on Vice City skyscraper roofs marked H on the map, reached by the lobby elevator, on a hotel roof at Ocean Beach, on the hospital roof and on a helipad east of Hamlet. TheGamer warns that those on the tallest towers tend to carry advanced trackers.||

blocks.title: Jets and airliners
blocks.text: ||Airliners stand at Vice City International Airport, where crossing the restricted gate brings three stars and some planes are locked. Jets are at Mile Zero Air Station, and taking one brings four stars. PowerPyx warns that jets taken from the airport carry trackers and bring fighter jets after you.||

blocks.title: The one plane you can keep
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says Kyle's Mallard, at Kyle McKittrick's farm in East Kelly County at the end of his side questline, can be kept and stays marked on the map wherever you leave it. The small planes at Wild Hog Point cannot be owned.||

blocks.caption: A red and white Buckingham Maverick helicopter in flight against the sky.

blocks.title: Before you take off
items: ||Every aircraft uses fuel, and PowerPyx notes that jets burn it faster than a crop duster.||
||GameSpot warns that flying a stolen aircraft through restricted airspace is an easy way to reach six stars.||
||At the edge of the map an aircraft runs out of fuel and crashes.||

blocks.text: Driving, fuel
How cars handle and how else you get around, as TGG reports it. He did not drive himself.

blocks.title: Weight
blocks.text: Nelson told him the team kept the best of Grand Theft Auto IV's feel with Grand Theft Auto V's accessibility. In the demo a muscle car spun out under hard acceleration.

blocks.title: Off-road
blocks.text: Fast cars and bikes reach higher top speeds than before. A supercar handles badly off the road.

blocks.title: Fuel
blocks.text: Cars need fuel. A gas station offers a repair or a fill; you hold R2 while the character fills up. Electric vehicles can be charged. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms fuel: it counts 57 gas stations, says every vehicle burns fuel and stops when the tank is empty, and says nearby stations are flagged on the map when fuel runs low. It does not cover charging or the controls.||

blocks.title: Mod shops
blocks.text: No single shop does everything. Each has a speciality, such as off-road builds or lowriders. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms it: it lists 14 mod shops, each tied to one kind of vehicle, for example retro cars, muscle cars or sports bikes.||

blocks.title: Your partner drives
blocks.text: You can swap between driver and passenger in a free-roam chase, and tell a partner at the wheel to hurry.

blocks.title: Buses and rides
blocks.text: You can take a bus or a ride and skip the journey. TGG relays Edge magazine's preview that buses keep to routes and times. ||PowerPyx's launch guide confirms the ride: a Paradise Taxi or a RydeMe car will skip the trip for $100, and there is no fast travel from the map itself. The launch entries read do not cover buses.||

items: Whether an overturned car can be rocked back onto its wheels: one creator says not, and TGG could not check.

chapters.title: Activities & Pastimes
chapters.intro: Things to do between missions as Rockstar showed them before launch, followed by the other activities in the Encyclopedia whose entries are not spoilers. Fishing and hunting have a chapter of their own.

blocks.text: Racing:
blocks.sub: Forty races, thirteen challenges and the drone trials

blocks.text: The Extended Look showed a circuit race with a lap counter, a night street race with nitrous and an off-road race with bikes and cars together. ||Launch guides count 40 races in six groups.||

blocks.caption: An off-road buggy sliding through mud during a race.
||The six race groups, as PowerPyx lists them||
rows: ||Vice City: Salton, La Perle, Ocean Beach and Gloriana Key||
||8 dirt track and oval races, from an optional Chapter 2 job||
||Grayson, Redshaw's, Ranchers and Big Pine, in Lummox and Mariana counties||

blocks.title: Entering a race
blocks.text: ||Race starts show as blue map icons from about 100 metres away. IGN says people around each venue hand out races, that you pay an entry fee and either rent a car or bring an owned one of the exact class, and that a bronze opens the next race in a group. Its maximum payouts run from $1,500 to $6,000. Winning 30 races counts for the 100% checklist.||

blocks.title: Gellhorn and Boone
blocks.text: ||At Gellhorn International Raceway an introduction event opens Keep It PG, a five-race amateur series that leads on to the superbike and supercar races. Boone Speedway in Hamlet is a dirt oval that RacingNews.co says copies Ocala Speedway, north of Tampa.||

blocks.caption: The circuit at Gellhorn International Raceway.

blocks.title: Race challenges
blocks.text: ||Thirteen solo time trials and stunt runs award bronze, silver and gold: six at the Mud Club, trials at Ambrosia Raceway, Boone Speedway, the Gellhorn raceway and dragway and the Kalaga Cycling Trial, and stunt runs at Hamlet BMX and Waning Sands Motocross. Ten golds count for the 100% checklist.||

blocks.title: Drone time trials
blocks.text: ||Top Fun runs 42 drone time trials at 14 sites, three per site, each started from a van for a flat entry fee. Beat par on the first two at a site to open the third. IGN gives the prizes as $750, $1,500 and $3,000, or $73,500 for all 42. The Dalton Island site needs a boat or an aircraft to reach.||

blocks.caption: The Top Fun drone race site in Hamlet.

blocks.title: Stunts
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx tracks 397 stunts: 130 stunt jumps, 202 flights under bridges, 40 knife flights and 25 base jumps. Any 300 count for the 100% checklist.||
Sport:
blocks.sub: Games to play and ways to train

blocks.text: The Extended Look showed the gym, basketball, pool and mini golf. ||Several of them raise a lead's stats, and doing them with your partner counts as time together.||

blocks.caption: ||The five golf courses (PowerPyx and IGN)||
rows: ||Wild West mini golf, 18 holes, entry fee||

blocks.title: Golf
blocks.text: ||Two of the three mini golf courses count for the 100% checklist; the full courses do not. IGN says holes finished under par give Focus progress, that full-course holes have bronze, silver and gold stroke targets, and that Leaf Links is private property, so its security has to be avoided.||

blocks.caption: The Wild West course at Frontier Adventure Golf.

blocks.title: Pool
blocks.text: ||The world has 17 pool tables. Seven have an opponent, in places such as Skeeter's in Hamlet, Zotico's in Balsero, The Thirsty Wolf in Belville, Jacob's Tavern in Millport and Delights Cabaret in Port Gellhorn; IGN says the other ten are free solo tables. Beating five different opponents counts for the 100% checklist, and pool raises Focus.||

blocks.title: Basketball
blocks.text: ||There are 100 hoops around Leonida, about half of them in Vice-Dale County. IGN says each score adds Focus, capped at five gains per 30 minutes of real time, and that 10, 50 and 100 hoops unlock clothing and tattoos. Ninety count for the 100% checklist.||

blocks.title: Shooting ranges
blocks.text: ||Griffin Shooting Range in north-west Vice City has six courses with three medal tiers; Rodgers Ranch, north-east of Port Gellhorn, has six themed courses with four tiers, from Market to Alien. A $5 waiver pass opens the challenges and a missing weapon type can be rented for $10. Finishing or quitting any challenge permanently raises Focus.||

blocks.title: The gym
blocks.text: ||Weights raise Strength and treadmills or bikes raise Cardio, at home early on and at fitness studios that charge a membership; Game Rant names Venus Fitness in Vice City at $600. The Fitness app sets workout windows, and missing one loses progress. Train together at a gym and the lead you are not playing works out too.||

blocks.caption: A character doing a bench press on pink gym equipment in a fitness studio.

blocks.title: Protein after a workout
blocks.text: ||A protein shake from the fridge at home, or a protein bar from a fitness studio, straight after a workout shortens the wait for the next window, according to Push Square and PowerPyx.||

blocks.title: Meditation
blocks.text: ||Ten meditation spots hold 18 meditations, since most can be done once by each lead, and meditating at the same spot with both counts twice. Meditation raises Focus. The spot at Jason's house exists only in Chapter 1, and the last, at the peak of Mount Kalaga, appears after the others.||

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia meditating cross-legged on a grassy hill.

blocks.text: Nightlife:
blocks.sub: Strip clubs, bars and dancing

blocks.text: The Extended Look showed nightclubs, and Rockstar's launch screenshots named Delights Cabaret and The Rusty Anchor. ||Kotaku notes that the strip clubs remain, although street sex workers are gone.||

blocks.caption: A roadside building at night with a neon sign reading Delights Cabaret and cars in the car park.
||The three strip clubs||
rows: ||Downtown Vice City, next to The Vault on NE 7th Street||
||North Crosstown, just up the road from NINE1NINE||

blocks.title: Private dances
blocks.text: ||Game8 says a dancer can be greeted and paid $300 for a private dance, and that $50 tips during it extend the dance. Polygon says dances are paid in cash only and that Lucia can buy them too; PC Gamer says one can also be bought from the person at the entrance to the private rooms. Nothing beyond the private dance is for sale.||

blocks.title: Bring cash
blocks.text: ||Private dances are cash only, Polygon says; the clubs have ATMs.||

blocks.title: Which club is which
blocks.text: ||GameSpot calls NINE1NINE the most luxurious, modelled on Miami's E11EVEN and with outrageous bar prices, and Delights the only club outside Vice City and more middle-class. Jack of Hearts, a hip-hop club on several floors, stays locked until a Chapter 3 story mission and, GameSpot says, sells private dances only at certain times. PC Gamer found stage dancing at Delights but not at NINE1NINE.||

blocks.caption: Boobie Ike and a companion standing outside a club at night under its red neon Jack of Hearts sign.

blocks.title: Drinks and dancing
blocks.text: ||Polygon says the clubs serve bar drinks with temporary stat boosts, and that dancing together there can improve Jason and Lucia's relationship; IGN also lists dancing together at clubs among the things that raise it.||

blocks.title: Bars
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's map tracks 122 bars, 60 of them in Ocean Beach alone, many of them hotel pool and rooftop bars. Some have a pool table with an opponent, and Press Start says bars and venues hold cabinets of Bang For Your Buck, a light-gun hunting arcade game.||

blocks.caption: A bar with a sign reading The Rusty Anchor, people on its porch and a man asleep on a picnic table.

blocks.title: The Vault and the casino
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says scanning a poster at The Vault nightclub Downtown unlocks The Vault Radio, one of two unique playlists. Merlin's Palace Casino stands in Balsero, but Game8 says its interior is closed and there are no casino games.||
Off duty:
blocks.sub: Diving, the water, video games and small pleasures

blocks.text: Jet skis, kayaking and scuba diving were all in the Extended Look, with the Keys as their natural home. TGG noted that scuba diving has an oxygen meter.

blocks.title: Treasure diving
blocks.text: ||A treasure hunter with a shop in Key Lento, Kenton Rees, sends you diving on shipwrecks after the Chapter 1 mission Island Dreams, which hands over scuba gear, a speargun and an underwater metal detector. His dive sites show as purple chest icons, and IGN says he pays $400 a doubloon where pawn shops pay $200. PowerPyx counts seven treasure sets, five of them for the 100% checklist.||

blocks.caption: The Scuba Gear prompt at the stern of a charter boat.

blocks.title: Scuba gear on board
blocks.text: ||Any boat you dive from needs scuba gear aboard. IGN says Kenton's boat and the boat at Jason's house always carry it.||

blocks.title: Jet skis, kayaks and the open sea
blocks.text: Rockstar's images show jet skis in the Keys and a kayaker at Mount Kalaga, and the Ultimate Edition gives Jason a Crest kayak at his safehouse. ||GameSpot names kayaking among the things the couple can do together, and says a jet ski heading far out to sea runs out of fuel and leaves the rider stranded.||

blocks.title: Parachuting
blocks.text: Parachuting appeared in the Extended Look. ||PowerPyx counts 25 base jumps from tall buildings among the stunts, and one Vehicle challenge asks you to parachute from an aircraft into the orca or dolphin tank at the Vice City Oceanarium.||

blocks.caption: The golden dome of the Vice City Oceanarium on the waterfront below downtown towers.

blocks.title: Video games at home
blocks.text: ||Four games can be played: Tenebrae Lux, Street Trash III and Time Jackers Rewind on the JoySystem console at home, and Bang For Your Buck on arcade cabinets. IGN says all four play on the home console after the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui. PowerPyx says the console cannot be used during Chapter 2.||

blocks.caption: Two characters on a couch playing a game on the TV.

blocks.title: Pets
blocks.text: Petting a dog was shown before launch. ||IGN says friendly cats and dogs can be praised, petted and fed up to two treats bought at grocery and convenience stores, which gives a small Focus boost.||

blocks.title: Fixing up the house
blocks.text: ||Jason's Key Lento house has optional repair jobs marked with paintbrush icons: the bedroom wall (which can then be painted), the outdoor steps, the leaky roof and the railing. Doing them before Lucia arrives improves the relationship. Eurogamer and Push Square count five jobs; GameSpot counts four.||

blocks.title: Ultimate Edition jobs
blocks.text: The Ultimate Edition adds a raid on the PTT Youngin$ compound in Southside Vice City, and Wyman's Classic Car Collection commission: find abandoned classics and unfinished project cars and restore them. ||PowerPyx and IGN list five classics restored through Wyman's questline.||

chapters.title: Money & Businesses
chapters.intro: Where money is kept, how it is earned and lost, who buys stolen goods and cars, and what there is to spend it on.

blocks.text: Where money
blocks.sub: The bank, the pocket and the bag

blocks.text: Money sits in three places: the bank, the cash you carry, and stolen goods you have not sold yet. Only the bank is safe.
Rob Nelson told IGN that money matters more in this story than in earlier games, and that at times you have to go out and earn it before the story moves on.

blocks.title: Three figures
blocks.text: TGG reports three amounts on screen: the bank balance, the cash you are carrying, and the value of loot you have not sold. ||Push Square's guide says both balances are shown by pressing Down on the D-pad.||

blocks.title: The bank account
blocks.text: ||The account comes from the banking app BuckMe, set up in the Chapter 1 mission Buck Me. GamesRadar+ says each lead has a personal checking account. PowerPyx says purchases come out of the bank even with no cash in your pocket, and that anything over $1,000 can only be paid through the app.||

blocks.title: Pocket cash
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson said before launch that cash you carry is at risk when you are Wasted or Busted. ||GamesRadar+ says each lead can carry up to $20,000, that aggressive civilians can take it, and that all of it is lost when Wasted or Busted. Pocket cash only covers purchases up to $1,000.||

blocks.title: ATMs
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG that putting cash in the bank means going to an ATM. ||GamesRadar+ says an ATM is used with Triangle (Y on Xbox) and offers Deposit, Withdraw and recent transactions, up to $20,000 at a time. The ATM Finder at the bottom of the BuckMe app routes you to the nearest one, and ATMs are also listed in the Personal section of the map index.||

blocks.title: Family Savings
blocks.text: ||GameSpot describes a savings pot shared by the two leads, whose goals bring better interest and strengthen their relationship. PowerPyx says money put into it is gone for good and not returned even after the story, but that saving there is how the checking account limit rises. DayOne's review says reaching each chapter's savings target pays a reward.||

blocks.title: Account limits
blocks.text: ||Rockstar Support says the limits on the BuckMe Checking and Family Savings accounts rise only as the main story goes on. A payment that cannot land because the checking account is full goes through once the account is upgraded. Rockstar gives no dollar figures.||

blocks.caption: ||Savings tiers in the Save for the Future task, run from the BuckMe app, as PowerPyx lists them. It says Premium is given automatically at the start of Chapter 4; GamesRadar+ says a Premium account can be signed up for from Chapter 3. A Shopping challenge, Nest Egg, asks for $1,500,000 banked in checking.||

blocks.title: Bank it early
blocks.text: ||IGN advises depositing cash at an ATM as soon as the bank account is set up in Chapter 1, together with any cash stashed in the safehouse bedroom, because carried cash is lost when you die.||

blocks.caption: The BuckMe app on the phone, showing a $100 balance and the Buck Yourself transfer option.
The BuckMe app's ATM finder

pages.title: What You Keep, What You Lose

blocks.text: Keep and
blocks.sub: What survives a bad day, and a new chapter

blocks.text: Being Wasted or Busted costs what you carry. Moving on to a new chapter can cost more than that.

blocks.title: Wasted or Busted
blocks.text: ||Game Rant says you come round nearby and lose your pocket cash, vehicles that were not saved, weapons you picked up instead of buying, and any stash bags. Owned vehicles and owned weapons are kept, lost cash does not come back, and neither the relationship nor the criminal profile changes. GamesRadar+ says the game autosaves at that point.||

blocks.title: Is the bank safe?
blocks.text: ||Push Square and IGN's beginner's guide say money in BuckMe is not touched. IGN's own Wanted guide disagrees: it says a small amount comes out of checking as well, and that surrendering costs the same. No guide read gives a hospital bill, a fine or a bribe.||

blocks.title: The car and its trunk
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a personal vehicle you are driving when Wasted or Busted is impounded, and GameSpot says bags left in an impounded car are lost. IGN says the trunk can hold stored weapons and goods such as drugs, jewelry and marked bills, so it pays to fetch the car quickly. Scooter Bros fetches it for a fee; IGN adds that climbing the impound fence and breaking out through the gate costs nothing, and police are only told that a vehicle was taken.||

blocks.title: Chapter 1 money
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's money guide says saving up during Chapter 1 is pointless, because the money is lost when the chapter ends. GTABase says Jason's first truck is also replaced later, losing any upgrades bought for it.||

blocks.title: Homes left behind
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says each chapter is built around a different safehouse and an earlier one cannot be revisited without an older save. It adds that the fishing boat behind Jason's house in Key Lento cannot be recovered once the story leaves Key Lento, and that story progress seems to clear unowned vehicles from where they were left. IGN says the Key Lento fences are not available in Chapter 2.||

blocks.title: Family Savings across the story
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx describes the savings pot two ways: its Buck Me page says money moved there can never be withdrawn or lost, and its tips page says it is gone for good and not returned after the story. Both agree it cannot be taken back out.||

blocks.title: Lost for good
items: ||Pocket cash, when Wasted or Busted.||
||Weapons picked up, not bought.||
||Stash bags left in a car that is impounded.||
||The last unowned vehicle you left behind, and anything in its trunk, if it is destroyed (GamesRadar+).||

blocks.title: Save at chapter ends
blocks.text: ||Missions cannot be replayed and there is no chapter select. PowerPyx suggests a manual save at the start and end of each of the five chapters, 10 of the 15 slots, because some optional missions close as the story moves on.||

blocks.caption: Jason crouched at a hidden wall stash at home, with a prompt to store cash.

frames.label: Busted

blocks.text: Earning by
blocks.sub: What pays, and when it opens

blocks.text: Nelson told TGG that at some points the story needs a cash amount before it moves on, and that how you earn it is up to you. What pays best changes with each chapter.

blocks.caption: Rockstar artwork of a masked Jason and Lucia holding guns during a bank robbery.
||The main earners chapter by chapter, from PowerPyx's money guide and its other launch-day guides. Robbery takes are covered in Robberies & Stealing.||

blocks.title: The quickest money
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's money guide calls bank vaults the fastest earner once they open at the end of Chapter 4: up to $205,000 for about five minutes' work.||
Side earnings

blocks.title: Races
blocks.text: ||IGN's racing pages give a buy-in of $150 to $400, plus a rental of $100 to $300 unless you bring an owned car of the exact class. Top payouts run from $1,500 to $6,000, paid by finishing position and medal. PC Gamer's figure for the Ambrosia oval, over $3,000, is higher than IGN's $1,900.||

blocks.title: Drone races
blocks.text: ||IGN says each Top Fun site pays $750, $1,500 and $3,000 for its three races, after a flat entry fee with free retries: $73,500 for all 42.||

blocks.title: Hunting to order
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG that hunting can earn money through a character who knows Jason. ||PowerPyx says the jobs are Jason's only, that the first pays $500 and that clean head or heart shots pay more. PC Gamer reports $2,500 for a large boar, and says smaller kills are bought straight from the trunk at the buyer's building.||

blocks.title: Treasure and cards
blocks.text: ||IGN says Kenton, the diving contact in Key Lento, pays $400 a doubloon where pawn shops pay $200. PowerPyx says collectible cards sell at pawn shops for about $20 to more than $1,000 by rarity, and a sold card still counts as collected.||

blocks.title: Found along the way
blocks.text: ||IGN points to a small plane that comes down south of Hamlet early on, leaving a pistol and drugs that can go straight to a Key Lento fence, with armed men soon arriving. Parked police cars can hold guns, ammunition, armor and sometimes money (Sportskeeda).||

blocks.title: Robberies
blocks.text: Stick ups, smash 'n' grabs, payday loan stores, banks, vaults and gang operations each have their own pages in Robberies & Stealing.

blocks.caption: Kenton's charter dock in Key Lento, where treasure is sold.

blocks.text: Fences and
blocks.sub: Turning loot into money

blocks.text: Stolen goods are worth nothing until somebody buys them. TGG reports that loot cannot be spent until a fence buys it or it is laundered, and that drugs, jewelry and cars go to different fences.
In IGN's demo, a fence who will buy shows on the map in green with a dollar sign.

blocks.caption: ||The seven fences in PowerPyx's guide, with what each pays best for. Locations and opening points from PowerPyx and IGN.||
rows: ||Lockup near the south-west tip of Key Lento||
||Stash bags, at lower prices than Donnie (IGN)||
||Trailer in the middle of Key Lento||
||Narcotics, at low rates; jewelry and bills very low||
||Narcotics and jewelry, low; marked bills very low||
||Jewelry and marked bills, high; narcotics medium||

blocks.title: Three kinds of goods
blocks.text: ||IGN says fences buy Narcotics, Jewelry and Marked Bills, and hovering over a fence on the map shows what it pays for each. TheSixthAxis's review says prices follow demand.||

blocks.title: Handing goods over
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says goods are dropped at the fence's container. IGN says the Key Lento lockup opens with the code 7700 and the bag goes in a yellow crate inside; in Port Gellhorn the goods go in the trunk of the fence's car and he pays through BuckMe. Later, a garage lets you leave goods for a chosen fence to collect.||

blocks.title: Marked bills
blocks.text: ||Cash from banks, payday loan stores, ATMs and security trucks is marked. PowerPyx says a fence will only take it once you have the Dye Pack Jammer, which comes with the Chapter 3 mission Credit Check, and that fencing $250,000 of it counts for the 100% checklist and a trophy.||

blocks.title: Fences who give work
blocks.text: TGG reports that fences pass on information, such as a safe code by text, and that working for them unlocks more. ||PowerPyx says the Port Gellhorn dealer later phones with robbery tips, the Little Cuba fence commissions jewelry, ATM and payday loan jobs and then sells security-van tips for $10,000, and the La Perle fence sends Jason after drug labs.||

blocks.title: Pawn shops
blocks.text: ||IGN says pawn shops, marked with green scales, buy collectible cards and underwater finds such as meteorites and doubloons. The nearest early one is in southern Hamlet.||

blocks.title: Who is open when
blocks.text: ||IGN says the Key Lento fences close in Chapter 2. PowerPyx says the Port Gellhorn dealer is unavailable for part of the story, and that the car buyers and the Vice City fences stay open after it.||

frames.label: A trunk drop-off

blocks.text: Sell or keep
blocks.sub: Car buyers, registration and delivery

blocks.text: Hold the phone's scanner over a car and Nelson says it shows whether the car is locked, alarmed or tracked, what it would fetch, and what registering it would cost. The tracker decides who will buy it.

blocks.caption: Lucia walking between a green and a red sports car inside a car buyer's garage.
||Who buys which car, from PowerPyx's guides. Its money guide gives $30,000 or more for a wish-list car in perfect condition; its fence guide says about $35,000 or more.||

blocks.title: The first buyer's rules
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says Moses will not take a car stolen close to his garage or one with any tracker. PC Gamer says he wants older, low-profile cars, pays from one to a few thousand dollars, and will not take another car for a while after each sale; PowerPyx puts the wait at about two minutes.||

blocks.title: Cars to order
blocks.text: ||After the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver, which pays $1,250 plus $500 for good condition, Moses texts for six particular cars, each paying $1,400 to $6,310 plus a condition bonus. When all six are delivered he leaves a unique Sultan in the small garage beside his shop, which can be sold or kept.||

blocks.title: Condition pays
blocks.text: Nelson said a damaged car earns less and can be repaired first. ||TheSixthAxis's review adds a bonus for a car delivered in mint condition. The first high-end delivery, in Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS, pays $21,250 plus $10,000 if the car arrives in good condition (PowerPyx).||

blocks.title: Selling at a Pay 'n' Spray
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a Stored Vehicles tab inside the shop also sells registered or garaged cars, that the scanner shows which buyers are interested, and that a dedicated car buyer may pay more for an exotic car. DayOne's review says only a set number of cars can be sold each day.||

blocks.title: The wish list
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's trophy guide names 16 cars on the high-end list; its money guide says 18. Any matching car taken off the street counts, the scanner shows whether a car is on the list, and Push Square says talking to the buyer at Leonida Auto World sometimes gives a hint.||

blocks.title: Keeping it instead
blocks.text: Before launch Nelson said the scanner shows what registering a car as your own would cost. ||PowerPyx says registration opens with Moses in Chapter 2 for cars without trackers, and at any Pay 'n' Spray for standard trackers early in Chapter 3. GameSpot says Moses discounts the first one, that later fees can reach tens of thousands, and that a tracked car cannot be modified until registered. A free parking slot is needed: PowerPyx says you start with one, GTABase three, GameSpot four.||

blocks.title: Delivery and recovery
blocks.text: TGG heard a phone app called Scooter Bros that brings your car and recovers it if destroyed. ||PowerPyx says it arrives after the mission Moses and charges a small fee; Push Square ties the fee to distance and condition. A $12,500 Premium upgrade gives three free deliveries a day, five with GTA+ according to IGN, plus one free impound retrieval.||

blocks.title: Two figures for 100%
items: ||PowerPyx's 100% guide says $200,000 of fenced vehicles counts toward the checklist. IGN's Vehicles guide (updated 11:35 a.m. PT, November 19) says $100,000. Neither has been checked in play for this manual.||

frames.label: The delivery app

blocks.text: What money
blocks.sub: Garages, shops, services and GTA+

blocks.text: There is no business to buy or run. Money goes on garages, cars, clothes, guns and services.

Before launch TGG reported that it did not look as though you own and run businesses, and Nelson told him homes come through the story and cannot be bought. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms garages are the only property for sale.||

blocks.caption: ||The eight garages sold through the Vice City Real Estate app, which arrives after the Chapter 2 mission Daily Driver: one parking spot each, $160,000 in all (PowerPyx). Areas from GTABase. GameSpot prices Persistence Road at $9,500 and Vela Rota at $30,000. Buying all eight earns the Little Boxes trophy.||

blocks.title: Garages you are given
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists four more from the story: Port Gellhorn Station (one spot, after Daily Driver), Thompson Court (two, Chapter 4), NE 15th Street (two, Chapter 5) and Pegassi Residences (three, Chapter 5), for 18 vehicle slots at most. GTABase lists a pre-order garage on Shore Drive and an Ultimate Edition garage in Watson Bay.||

blocks.title: What a garage does
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says a garage also lets you manage weapons, change loadout, raise Focus and drop off goods for sale, that garages can be bought by visiting them, and that none is in Lummox County.||

blocks.title: GTA+
blocks.text: Rockstar's GTA+ page lists four perks for members on console: the '90 Annis Venturas BLVD Elegy with a garage in Crosstown, claimable from Chapter 3; 10 percent more money when selling owned vehicles; transit bonuses, among them Scooter Bros Premium and premium RydeMe; and 10 percent off at selected businesses such as weapon and clothes shops, hairdressers, tattooists and mod shops. An active membership and an internet connection are needed. ||Polygon says the Crosstown garage has a weapon locker and can fence stolen goods, and the perks last only while the membership is active.||

blocks.title: Looking the part
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 67 clothing stores in five types and 17 footwear stores, 18 hair and beauty salons, and 11 tattoo studios, each with its own style. Game Rant gives a gym membership at Venus Fitness as $600. Shopping challenges ask for over $5,000 spent on clothes and over $1,000 at salons.||

blocks.title: Running a car
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 14 mod shops, each for a kind of vehicle, and 19 Pay 'n' Sprays that repair, repaint, register and buy. GamesRadar+ says gas stations only patch minor damage and charge more. GameSpot reports pump prices in Key Lento of $4.29 a gallon for unleaded and $5.22 for diesel. Shopping challenges ask for over $20,000 in one mod-shop visit and $125,000 in all.||

blocks.title: Rides
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says Paradise Taxi takes pocket cash while RydeMe fares come out of BuckMe. PowerPyx says $100 on top of the fare skips the journey.||

items: ||Impound fees, hospital bills, and salon or tattoo prices: no guide read gives them.||
||Buying a car outright. GTABase's map marks Baller and Vapid dealerships in Southside, but no guide read describes buying from them.||
||Gambling. Game8 says the casino in Balsero cannot be entered and there are no casino games.||

chapters.title: Robberies & Stealing
chapters.intro: Stores, banks, jewelry and cars: what can be taken, what it takes to take it, and who buys it afterwards.

blocks.text: Robberies
blocks.sub: How the pair make their money

blocks.text: Rob Nelson calls robberies a huge part of what you can, and need to, do between story missions. You can rob as Jason and Lucia together or alone.

blocks.caption: Two characters tie bandanas over their faces at a door marked Open 7 Days.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:28

blocks.text: You can rob pretty much anything.

The callout is Nelson's phrase. The targets he names are shops, banks and payday loan places, and in the demo he points at a shop that sells headphones as somewhere you could rob. ||PowerPyx's launch guides list all three in the released game, along with jewelry stores, pawn shops and gang operations. The next page sets them side by side.||
Robbery, as the footage shows it

blocks.title: Cover your face
blocks.text: At a glass door marked Open 7 Days, both characters tie bandanas over their faces before going in.

blocks.title: Go in armed
blocks.text: In a convenience store, one of them walks the aisles while the other goes to the counter and leans over it. The display shows a pistol in hand, and a sign by the door reads "Smile, you're on camera".
blocks.frameAlt: A character walking through a convenience store towards the counter, with the wanted display at the top right
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:48

blocks.title: The police are told
blocks.text: The wanted display is already showing inside the store: two gray stars and five Heat icons, among them a camera and a pistol. ||IGN's launch guide says gray stars mean a crime has been reported and police are on their way with a description but have not seen you.||

blocks.title: Get out
blocks.text: They leave by the front door. The footage cuts away before a getaway is shown.
These are short clips cut together, and the door and the store may not be the same place. They show what a robbery can look like, not a set of rules.
What can
||Launch guides sort robbery targets into a handful of kinds, each opening at a different point in the story and paying in a different form.||

blocks.caption: Lucia holds up the teller at a store counter while bystanders stand nearby.

blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide to the in-game progress menu says it groups robberies into 11 kinds but itemises seven: convenience stores, liquor stores, fast food joints, jewelry stores, pawn shops, payday loans and bank jobs. Gang operations sit under the same Robberies filter on the map.||

blocks.caption: ||Counts, unlock points and takes are PowerPyx's, from launch day, and are one guide's figures. Its two pages disagree on stick ups: the completion checklist counts 91 and the progress database adds up to 109. Takes are a range for one robbery, not a total.||
rows: Stick ups (convenience, liquor and fast food stores)
Not given in the guides read
Up to $25,000 at the best stores
An optional job late in Chapter 4
Not given in the guides read
Not given in the guides read

blocks.title: Check the card first
blocks.text: ||GameSpot and Eurogamer say hovering over a robbery on the map shows its potential take and its security level. The card in one PowerPyx screenshot calls Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds a large, low-end jewelry store with medium security and a take of $4,500 to $12,000. Eurogamer calls banks the hardest places to rob.||
blocks.frameAlt: The in-game map with the Richardson Jewelry & Diamonds robbery card, showing its security and take value

blocks.title: What counts as done
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says a jewelry store or pawn shop counts only once its back-room safe is looted, a small bank only once both the cash drawer and the safe are emptied, and a gang operation only once every key valuable is taken. Gang operations show a yellow Robbery Opportunity icon until visited and later restock.||

blocks.title: Who points you at targets
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says Dunk, a fence in Port Gellhorn, later phones with robbery tips that mark two places on the map, and that Yasmani in Little Cuba asks for pieces from particular jewelry stores and then offers ATM and payday loan jobs. ATMs, it says, have to be pulled out of the wall with a car fitted with a winch.||

blocks.caption: The map's Robberies list open on Bank Jobs, with the card for the small Fleeca bank in Key Lento listing take value, cash drawer and safe.

blocks.title: Robbing for the challenge list
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and DayOne list two Criminal challenges for store robberies: three stores in a day, and two stores in each of the five counties inside 20 minutes, both without dying or being arrested.||
Safes, alarms
||The back room is where most of a store's take is kept. Launch guides describe how its safe, its alarm and its camera recordings work.||

blocks.caption: A robbery under way inside a jewelry store.

blocks.title: Safe codes change
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says safe codes are randomised: they differ between players and change even when the same shop is robbed twice, so published lists of codes do not help.||

blocks.title: Where the code is
blocks.text: Before launch, Nelson told TGG a fence may text you a code, or it may be somewhere in the store. ||GameSpot says a code can be on a guard or nearby, and that in banks it turns up on sticky notes, computer screens or downed guards.||

blocks.title: No code
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says that without a code small safes can be picked, lockboxes snapped open with the Snap Gun, and nearly all safes forced. IGN says safes and locked doors in banks, payday loan stores and jewelry stores open only to a Sticky Bomb planted through the on-screen prompt; a thrown one does nothing, and planting one on an alarmed door sets the alarm off.||

blocks.title: The alarm panel
blocks.text: Before launch, Nelson described a quiet tool for the back door and an alarm system that can be disabled. ||GameSpot says the Snap Gun opens locked doors without setting off the alarm, and that once the alarm panel is switched off, display cases can be smashed without triggering it.||
blocks.frameAlt: The front of The Siren's Chest jewelry store

blocks.title: Camera recordings
blocks.text: TGG relayed a preview of a shop that kept its footage in the cloud. ||IGN confirms two kinds of camera Heat: a camera icon means the footage is stored on site and can be destroyed, and a cloud icon means it cannot be reached. IGN says bank jobs most often show the cloud. GameSpot puts the recordings in the back room.||

blocks.title: Slip out or clear the cases
blocks.text: ||GTABase says that at two of Yasmani's jewelry stores you can leave quietly once the safe is open, or go into the front of the shop and empty the display cases for more money.||

blocks.title: Quiet robberies and the profile
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the Professional criminal profile comes from stealth, harming no one in robberies, destroying tapes and disabling alarms.||
The pawn shop
In IGN's interview Nelson robs a pawn shop without preparing, and says what he should have done.

blocks.caption: Inside a jewelry store during a robbery in the footage.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:00

blocks.title: Prepare
blocks.text: Nelson says he should really be preparing, for example by putting a vehicle out front. He goes in without. ||Push Square's review of the released game makes the same point: a robbery can end without a chase if you scout the target, change outfit and pick a getaway vehicle to suit the job.||

blocks.title: Two people, two jobs
blocks.text: IGN describes Nelson, as Jason, heading to the back to look for a safe while Lucia keeps things under control by the door. ||GamesRadar+ says the partner can also be told to wait in the car during a robbery or to come in as backup.||

blocks.title: Open the safe
blocks.text: He finds the safe, then tracks down its combination. He also carries an explosive, which he says would damage some of the take. ||PowerPyx's launch guides describe using sticky bombs, sold at Ammu-Nation, to blow open back-room safes. They do not say whether that costs you part of the take.||

blocks.text: With police gathering at the front, he leaves by a back door.

blocks.title: Masks
blocks.text: If the police were told about a masked person, taking the mask off afterwards makes you harder to recognise. Nelson's advice, in translation: get out of the car and take it off. ||GameSpot gives the same routine for the released game: a hat and bandana put on before the crime and taken off after. PowerPyx says the bandana, glasses and hat are switched from the item wheel.||

blocks.title: Sell what you took
blocks.text: A fence who will buy shows green with a dollar sign on the map. The pair have jewelry to sell him. ||IGN says hovering over a fence on the map shows what it pays for each kind of goods.||

blocks.title: A getaway in the footage
blocks.text: After the jewelry store, two characters leave on a motorcycle, the passenger carrying a duffel bag. The stars at that moment are hollow.
blocks.frameAlt: Two characters on a motorcycle at a junction, the passenger carrying a duffel bag
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:06

blocks.text: Banks
Bank robbery was shown in Rockstar's own artwork long before launch. ||Launch guides split banks into small branches and large banks with a vault, and both pay in marked bills.||

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia in bandanas with guns inside a Fleeca bank as staff raise their hands.

blocks.title: Small banks
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 14 small branches of Fleeca, Shorefront, Lombank, Gibson Brothers Bank and Druthers State Bank. Each has a cash drawer and a safe, and it takes $5,000 to $45,000 depending on the branch.||

blocks.title: Marked bills
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says cash from banks and payday loan stores comes as marked bills, which a fence will only take once you have the Dye Pack Jammer. The in-game equipment list says the jammer disables exploding dye packs. Both arrive partway through Chapter 3.||

blocks.title: Vaults open for deliveries
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says a vault cannot be picked or blown open. It opens only briefly while an armoured truck makes a delivery, and PowerPyx describes tailing a security van to the bank and getting in while the guard carrying the cash case is inside.||

blocks.title: Tips on the vans
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says vaults open up through an optional job late in Chapter 4. After that, and once two payday loan stores have been robbed for him, Yasmani sells tips on where the vans are for $10,000; a tip marks the vans with a purple icon.||

blocks.title: Four stars at once
blocks.text: ||Every guide read that covers vaults says the same: robbing one brings four wanted stars immediately. PowerPyx gives takes of about $65,000 to $205,000, the highest at two Lombank branches.||

blocks.caption: Lucia aiming a pistol inside a Fleeca bank branch.
||The eight large banks with vaults and the take PowerPyx gives for each vault robbery. No other guide read lists them.||

items: ||Guards: PowerPyx says nothing about who guards each branch.||
||How long a vault stays open during a delivery. GameSpot says only that it is brief.||

Before launch, Nelson named a slim jim, a key cloner and a quiet way through a back door. ||The released game's Equipment list has those and more, and almost all of them come from the story, not from a shop.||

blocks.caption: The in-game Equipment menu with the pry bar's icon highlighted and its description.

blocks.text: ||Guides name the job differently. PowerPyx says the cloner is given at the start of the Chapter 3 mission Clonin' Keys, Makin' GS; PC Gamer and Gamer Guides call the mission Steal the Zorruso, given by Randy; GameSpot says Randy hands it over around the halfway point of the story.||

blocks.title: Using the Key Cloner
blocks.text: ||PC Gamer says you stand at a keyless car's door, choose Clone Key and use the control stick to find a sweet spot that speeds it up. GameSpot adds that no hot-wiring is needed afterwards, and Gamer Guides says the app both opens and starts the car.||

Whether a crew can be hired for robberies outside the story. ||PowerPyx's walkthrough groups a run of preparation missions under each story heist; nothing read describes hiring help for open-world robberies.||

Stolen goods are not money until somebody buys them. TGG reported before launch that drugs, jewelry and cars each go to a different fence. ||Launch guides name seven fences and the rates each pays.||

blocks.title: Bags, not cash
blocks.text: TGG reported that loot carried in a duffel bag shows as its own figure and cannot be spent until it is sold. ||PowerPyx says each lead carries two stash bags, so the pair can carry four, and that a bag is passed to the partner with Hand Over Bag. GameSpot says a van or truck holds upwards of eight and a motorcycle none; DayOne's review mentions up to six in a large trunk.||

blocks.title: The three kinds of goods
blocks.text: ||IGN says fences buy three kinds of goods, narcotics, jewelry and marked bills, and that hovering over a fence on the map shows its rates. TheSixthAxis's review says prices follow demand.||

blocks.caption: ||Who buys what, from PowerPyx's fence guide and IGN's. Car buyers are on the Trackers page. Rates are the guides' words, not figures.||

Low for narcotics and jewelry, very low for marked bills

blocks.title: How the drop-off works
blocks.text: ||Goods are left at the fence's own spot, not handed over. IGN describes a keypad lockup with a yellow crate for Brian, a green crate at Donnie's trailer, and the trunk of Dunk's car, who pays through BuckMe. PowerPyx and GameSpot say a garage later lets you drop goods off for a fence you choose.||

blocks.title: Fences come and go
blocks.text: ||IGN says the Key Lento fences are not available in Chapter 2, and PowerPyx says Dunk is out of reach for part of the story. All of them, it says, stay available after the story.||

blocks.title: Sending your partner
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ and GameSpot say a partner sent away after a robbery can sell the loot alone, possibly for less, with the money arriving after a delay.||

blocks.title: Loot is easy to lose
items: ||Game Rant says stash bags are lost when you are Wasted, and GamesRadar+ and GameSpot say bags left in a personal vehicle are lost if it is impounded. The Law Enforcement chapter covers both.||

blocks.text: Robbery
More on robbing stores, from TGG's account of the preview and the other previews he relays, with what launch guides now add.

blocks.caption: Two people in black, one in a skull mask, holding guns beside an open vault door with banknotes in the air.

blocks.title: Any store
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG you can try to rob any store you walk into. Small ones show no robbery icon; bigger targets can show their potential take on the map. ||PowerPyx counts convenience stores, liquor stores and fast food outlets together as stick ups.||

blocks.title: Heroes
blocks.text: Customers and staff may rush you, try to take your gun, or draw their own. TGG saw both happen.

blocks.title: Bags and vehicles
blocks.text: Loot goes into duffel bags, and there is a limit to how many you can take. A bike gets away fast; a van carries more. ||GameSpot puts numbers to it: upwards of eight bags in a van or truck, none on a motorcycle.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia carrying a pink duffel bag and holding a pistol outside a Checks Cashed storefront

blocks.title: Other people's robberies
blocks.text: He relays previews in which masked robbers had crashed and spilled their loot, and two robbers were trapped in a jewelry store.

blocks.title: Robbing in a mission
blocks.text: Where a mission turns into a robbery, Rockstar says it tries to keep it consistent with how robberies work in the open world.

items: Whether bystanders who fight back are more likely at some stores than others.
||The bag limit for each vehicle: GameSpot's and DayOne's numbers differ, and neither lists vehicles one by one.||

blocks.text: Stealing
Cars are worth money to fences, and some are harder to take and to keep than others.

blocks.title: Scan it first
blocks.text: The phone's scanner tells you whether a car is locked, alarmed or tracked, and what it is worth. In the demo it reports a car as locked, with an alarm and no tracker. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms the app in the released game: it shows a car's sale value, its registration fee and whether it has a tracker or keyless entry. GamesRadar+ says it also shows which fences are interested, and IGN says an upgraded scanner comes with the Chapter 2 mission Moses.||
blocks.frameAlt: A Riata pickup in Moses' lot at night with its WAiNK scan panel on screen

blocks.text: Edge, IGN and TGG give the scanner app's name as WAINK. ||PowerPyx's launch guides write it WAiNK and also use it for scanning places, and the 100% checklist asks for 100 WAiNK locations.||

blocks.title: Tools
blocks.text: Nelson names a slim jim, and a key cloner for newer and luxury cars that comes later. Some parked cars cannot be taken until you have the right tool; a car with a driver in it can always be carjacked. In translation, he adds that smashing a window sets off the alarm. TGG adds that the slim jim is worked with the analog sticks. ||Launch guides confirm both tools, covered on the Equipment page; TheSixthAxis's review says taking a parked car can need a keyless-entry app that the story unlocks.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia using a Slim Jim on the door of a brown SUV in Moses's yard

blocks.title: Taking one that is occupied
blocks.text: You can aim your weapon and tell people to get out of their car, without having to pull anybody out. TGG adds that a driver can resist, as a quick-time interaction, and he watched a passenger throw Nelson back out. ||TheSixthAxis's review says carjacking still works but draws the police.||
The footage shows it: a masked character aims a pistol at the driver of a car, and a second character then goes to the driver's door.

blocks.caption: A masked character aims a pistol at an occupied car.
blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:37

blocks.title: What it costs in stars
blocks.text: ||IGN lists stealing a car with no tracker as a one-star crime, and setting off a car's advanced tracker as two stars at once. PowerPyx says jets with advanced trackers bring four.||

blocks.title: Deliver it in good condition
blocks.text: A car fence pays less for a damaged car. Nelson says he can repair the car first. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: buyers pay more the better the condition, with a bonus for a car delivered in mint condition. IGN says Moses also texts requests for particular cars that pay extra.||

blocks.title: Your own car
blocks.text: Your personal vehicle can be called to you, and spare outfits can be kept in its trunk. ||GamesRadar+ says each lead has one personal vehicle at a time and that its trunk holds the loadout, outfits and stash bags; IGN says up to five outfits fit. TheSixthAxis's review says a registered car can be called up even when it has been impounded.||

blocks.title: Moses is choosy
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says Moses will not take a car stolen close to his garage, or one with any tracker, and IGN says the first car he asks for should be a low-key one, not a supercar or anything too modern.||
Trackers, buyers

A stolen car is sold or kept according to the tracker it carries. TGG reported before launch that a fence removes trackers, but only the levels you have unlocked with him. ||Launch guides describe the ladder from the selling side.||

blocks.title: The advanced tracker
blocks.text: A car with what Nelson calls an advanced tracker, shown by a blinking red light, gives its position to the police if it is driven slowly. TGG says it beeps faster as you slow down, then alerts the police. ||IGN says setting one off brings two stars at once.||

blocks.caption: ||Who takes which car, from PowerPyx and GamesRadar+. Prices are PowerPyx's, for one sale. PowerPyx's own pages disagree on Randy: its money guide says 18 cars on his list at $30,000 or more each, its page on Randy says 16 cars at roughly $35,000 or more.||

Once you have the Key Cloner
$30,000 to $35,000 or more in perfect condition

blocks.title: Selling limits
blocks.text: ||DayOne's review says only a set number of cars can be sold each day, and PowerPyx's money guide mentions a wait of about two minutes between sales to Moses. GamesRadar+ says a dedicated car fence may pay more for an exotic car than a Pay 'n' Spray.||

blocks.title: Registering a stolen car
blocks.text: ||A stolen car becomes your own once it is registered for a fee and there is a free slot. PowerPyx says Moses registers cars with no tracker from Chapter 2 and any Pay 'n' Spray registers cars with a standard tracker from Chapter 3. Push Square says registering swaps the plates and costs more the more the car is worth; DayOne says each tracker level costs more.||
blocks.frameAlt: A blue car inside a Pay 'n' Spray with the shop menu open and Register highlighted

blocks.title: Tracked cars cannot be modified
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says a car with a standard tracker cannot be modified until it is registered.||

blocks.title: Garages
blocks.text: Before launch, TGG reported that more garages can be bought and that you keep as many cars as you have spaces. ||PowerPyx says each parking spot lets one more vehicle be registered, up to 18 in all. GameSpot says a garage is also where goods can be dropped off for sale. The two guides disagree on how many slots you start with: PowerPyx says one, GameSpot four.||

items: ||Whether Randy's list holds 16 or 18 cars: PowerPyx gives both.||
||How many cars can be sold in a day: DayOne gives no number.||

chapters.title: Law Enforcement
chapters.intro: Stars, Heat and the police who keep what they learn: how a response starts, what they know, and how a chase ends.

blocks.text: Law
blocks.sub: The Heat System & Wanted Response

blocks.text: Law enforcement in Leonida is about more than outrunning the officer behind you. Rockstar describes police who keep hold of what they have learned about a suspect, so it matters what they know, not only whether they can see you.

blocks.caption: Jason on a motorcycle, a police vehicle close behind.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason Duval 11"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Losing sight of the police is not necessarily the same as losing their information.
Stars and Heat at a glance

Two things sit at the top right of the screen: up to six wanted stars, and beneath them a row of small red Heat icons. The stars are the wanted level. The icons are separate, and change while the stars stay the same.

blocks.caption: Lucia fires a rifle from the passenger seat of a convertible as police cars close in.

blocks.text: Rob Nelson says the icons show what the police know about you. In his demo they knew what he looked like, what he was wearing, what the pair were driving, and that they were a couple. A crime has to be seen by a witness, or set off an alarm, before it is reported at all. ||TheSixthAxis's review describes the released game the same way: witnesses can call the police, the police work from a description of you, and they know whether you are working alone or as a pair.||

blocks.caption: ||What the police know, and what to do about it, are from Nelson's interview, and TheSixthAxis's review confirms that changing your looks, clothing and vehicle stops you matching the description. Matching each to an icon is still this manual's reading of the footage, not a Rockstar statement.||
rows: Change your appearance: glasses, a hat, a haircut
Put on a different outfit, bought at a store or kept in your own car's trunk
Get out and take a different vehicle

blocks.caption: ||These two icons are in the footage. No source read names them, but TheSixthAxis's review supports the reading: it says security footage can be deleted and that weapons, like vehicles and clothing, can be changed or abandoned so you no longer match the description.||
rows: You were caught on a security camera
The police know which weapon was used

blocks.text: Rockstar North co-studio head Rob Nelson calls the mechanic the heat system, and describes police dispatch as very specific about what it knows.

The creator TGG, who previewed the game, quotes Nelson as saying the team wanted police to stop forgetting you the moment you lose them and to have "a bit more persistent memory." The quote comes from TGG's video, as reported by GamesRadar+; it is not in IGN's transcript.

||This chapter was written before release and has since been brought up to date from launch guides. IGN's guide gives a crime-by-crime, star-by-star account and GameSpot names six kinds of Heat; their accounts are added, spoiler-marked, on the pages that follow. The only timings given are GameSpot's, for five and six stars.||
The wanted

blocks.credit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 14:08

blocks.caption: A police helicopter during a three-star chase.

Playing the demo, Rob Nelson described one star as not a big deal: leave the area the police are responding to and you should generally be fine. He also said things escalate if you choose to escalate them.
When the stars are hollow, the police are responding without knowing who you are, and leaving the area is enough.

blocks.title: How the footage was read
items: Every picture of the wanted display in this chapter is a frame from Rockstar's own Extended Look, downloaded from Rockstar's media page.
The video was examined as still frames, a few seconds apart. Times are approximate, and anything that lasts less than a few seconds, or that only shows in motion, may have been missed.

blocks.title: About the pictures
items: The large photographs in this chapter are official Rockstar screenshots and artwork, or screenshots from launch guides, chosen for their subject. They are not evidence for the rule printed beside them.
The small pictures of the wanted stars and Heat icons from the Extended Look are different: they are frames from Rockstar's own footage, and the claims labelled R★ Verified rest on them.

blocks.text: The stars

Four different looks appear in Rockstar's footage. What each is seen alongside is recorded here. Before launch Rockstar described the meaning of only one of them. ||IGN's launch guide now explains five.||

blocks.title: Hollow stars
blocks.frameAlt: Two outlined stars at the right of six positions, with no icons beneath
blocks.text: About 18:04 to 18:11. Two outlined stars with dark centres and no Heat icons, as two masked characters get onto a motorcycle across the road from a jewellers. A few seconds earlier, inside a jewelry store, a camera icon shows on its own with no stars.
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 18:08

blocks.text: In his own demo, Nelson said hollow white stars mean the police do not know who you are: they head for the scene without a description, and leaving the area is enough. The outlined stars in this frame appear to be the same thing.

blocks.title: Gray stars
blocks.frameAlt: Two gray stars with five red icons beneath: camera, two heads, coat hanger, head, pistol
blocks.text: About 11:48 to 11:52, and again at about 12:08; frames in between show no wanted display. Two gray stars with five Heat icons beneath them. At 11:48 the scene is the inside of a convenience store. Read at six frames a second across seven seconds, the two stars stay gray throughout: they do not flash.
blocks.frameCredit: Frame from "Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look", Rockstar Games, about 11:48

blocks.text: One guide author, who did not attend the preview, believes gray stars mean the police hold information about you and are actively searching. No one who attended, and no one at Rockstar, mentions gray stars in the sources read.

blocks.title: White stars
blocks.frameAlt: Four white stars with four red icons beneath: two heads, coat hanger, head, car
blocks.text: About 14:04 to 14:32, and again 15:20 to 15:40, with no display for about 50 seconds between. Four white stars with four Heat icons: first while a character fires on a police pickup, then while driving a car.

blocks.title: Red stars
blocks.frameAlt: Four red stars with three red icons beneath: two heads, coat hanger, head
blocks.text: About 15:50 to 16:32. Four stars are red by about 15:50. By 15:53 the car is inside a parking garage; by 15:59 two characters are on foot beside it. The moment of the change from white is not in the frames examined.

Two solid white stars also appear later, at about 18:24 to 18:44, first with three icons and then with four. After the hollow stars at about 18:12, some twelve seconds of footage show no display at all, so a change from hollow to solid is not seen.
What launch guides say each look means

blocks.caption: ||IGN's explanations of the star looks in the released game. IGN does not mention flashing stars.||

An incident is known but not who did it, for example when Heat was cleared before you were seen, or gunfire was heard but not seen
Police can see you and are in full pursuit

How hollow stars become solid, and what turns white stars red: neither change is on screen in the frames examined.

blocks.text: How police
A response starts with somebody, or something, raising the alarm.

blocks.caption: Two masked people with guns at a counter while three others raise their hands.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Jason and Lucia 15"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.title: A witness
blocks.text: Nelson has said the wanted system needs someone to witness the crime for it to be reported. In his demo, a bystander called an incident in. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that witnesses can call the police.||

blocks.title: An alarm
blocks.text: The other route he names is an alarm being set off. ||IGN adds a third: a crime big enough for dispatch to respond at once, such as an explosion, trespassing in a high-security area or stealing a plane. It also says a mistaken report can bring the police.||

blocks.title: A vehicle tracker
blocks.text: Some cars carry what Nelson calls an advanced tracker, shown by a blinking red light. It tells the police where the car is if it is not driven fast enough. A scanner on the in-game phone can tell you beforehand whether a car is locked, alarmed or tracked. ||IGN says setting one off brings two stars at once.||

blocks.title: The phone in their hand
blocks.text: ||IGN says a person reaching for their phone to call the police can have it slapped out of their hand, though with many witnesses a call can still get through. People may also call the police on someone standing on their property.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason and Lucia walking into a convenience store, with a shopper and a cashier inside

blocks.title: A gun on show
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says a long gun in your hands makes people leave or turn hostile, and the police warn you first. ||IGN says a pistol can be hidden by switching to Unarmed, but a longarm stays strapped to your back and in view, so civilians may still call the police until it is stored.||

blocks.title: Do not read too much into this
items: Nelson was describing the open world. Missions and scripted events may behave differently.
Being noticed is not the same as being identified: see the next pages.

blocks.text: Heat:
Heat is the information the police hold about you. On screen it appears as small icons with the wanted stars.

blocks.caption: Lucia, with a patrol officer and police lights behind her.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Lucia Caminos 14"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Nelson points to icons on screen that show what the police know. In his demo they knew what he looked like, what he was wearing, what the pair were driving, and that they were a couple. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that the police work from a description of you and know whether you are alone or a pair.||
In the footage the icons are small red discs in a row beneath the stars. Six different ones appear: a camera, two heads, a coat hanger, a single head, a pistol and a car. Up to five show at once.

blocks.caption: Two close-ups of the wanted stars with the row of Heat icons beneath them, numbered 1 to 6.

blocks.text: One guide says the more icons are active, the harder the police are to lose.

||GameSpot's launch guide names six things the police use to identify you: appearance, outfit, visible weapon, vehicle, CCTV footage and your partner. They match the six icons in the footage. PowerPyx places the red icons in the top-right corner.||

blocks.title: Appearance
blocks.text: The police know what you look like. Glasses, a hat or a new haircut change your appearance, but not what you are wearing. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: you can change how you look so that you no longer match the description, and hats, sunglasses and masks can hide your face during a crime.||

blocks.title: Clothing
blocks.text: The police know your outfit. Nelson calls an outfit they have seen compromised. ||TheSixthAxis's review lists clothing among the things you can change or abandon to stop matching the description.||

blocks.title: Vehicle
blocks.text: The police know what you are driving. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that changing or abandoning the vehicle is one way to stop matching the description, and PowerPyx's guide says a Pay 'n' Spray repaints a vehicle so the police no longer recognise it.||
Evidence that can

blocks.caption: Jason and Lucia pull bandanas over their faces outside a Xero gas station at dusk.

blocks.title: Accomplice
blocks.text: The police can know that Jason and Lucia are together. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that the police know whether you are working alone or as a pair.||

blocks.title: Weapon
blocks.text: A pistol icon appears among the Heat icons at about 11:48.

Before launch, guides read the pistol icon as the police knowing which weapon was used. ||GameSpot's launch guide calls it a visible weapon, and its remedy is to put a pistol away and stow or drop a longarm; owned weapons that are dropped return to your vehicle's trunk on their own.||

blocks.text: Nelson uses "heat" in two ways: for what the police know about you, and for the police searching an area ("we have heat now"). This manual keeps the two apart, but the game may not.
The two can come apart. At one point in the demo Nelson notes that the pair have got away with no heat; shortly after, police searching the area means they have heat again.
GamesRadar+, reporting the creator TGG's preview, says clues can still get you recognised later, even after the wanted stars have gone.

||IGN's launch guide gives the distinction its own look on screen: red-outlined stars mean the police know a crime happened in the area but you no longer match the description, while solid red means they are still hunting someone who matches the Heat icons shown.||

blocks.text: Finding
You are expected to look for the police, not read them off the map.

blocks.text: Nelson describes Focus as much like Eagle Eye in Red Dead Redemption 2: a way to locate things you want to find, and certainly police. In IGN's account of the demo it made a nearby officer glow.

TGG also quotes Nelson as saying that police do not show up on the radar and do show up when you use Focus, and that this is harder but more fun, depending on the wanted level. Again this is TGG's account, reported by GamesRadar+.
That Focus shows police through walls is TGG's own description, not a Nelson quote. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus shows enemies in nearby rooms; it does not mention police specifically.||
One guide, reading the footage, suggests that at higher wanted levels the minimap is washed out by red and blue flashing light.

blocks.text: Hot
Getting away from the scene may not make the scene safe to come back to.

blocks.caption: Patrol cars gathered on a bridge, a boat with flashing lights below and a helicopter sweeping a searchlight overhead.
blocks.credit: Official Rockstar Games screenshot ("Vice City 17"), rockstargames.com/VI/media/screenshots

blocks.text: Checking the map in his demo, Nelson calls the place of an incident a hot area: the police are there and will hang around for a while, and the map still shows a star over it. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms that after an escape the wanted area stays marked on the map for a while.||

VICE, relaying creators' previews, calls it the active search area and says red stars mean you have escaped the chase but are still inside it. One guide describes a red zone with a lighter ring around it. What the game itself calls the area on screen is not confirmed.

||Launch guides confirm two areas. PowerPyx separates a flashing red and blue search area from a larger red heat zone around it. DayOne's review says each star widens the zone, and that the higher the level, the longer you have to stay away for it to clear. IGN says the area is outlined and shaded red on the map.||

blocks.title: Leave
blocks.text: At a low wanted level, getting out of the area the police are responding to is described as enough.

blocks.title: Wait
blocks.text: With police searching an area, one option Nelson lists is to wait for it to die down.

blocks.title: Coming back too soon
blocks.text: Nelson says that if you go back, the police will still be hanging around for a while.

One creator said before launch that he was told the search covers the whole map at the highest wanted level. ||IGN confirms it for six stars, and GameSpot says the areas involved stay watched until the character is caught or killed; going back in needs a full change of clothes, appearance and vehicle.||

items: The size of a hot area and how fast it shrinks. ||DayOne says only that each star widens it.||

Whether a change of outfit clears heat while you are still inside a hot area: published accounts differ. ||PowerPyx says a respray removes vehicle heat only once you are outside the immediate search area.||

Each clue has its own answer. Most of these come from Rob Nelson's own demo; none is a guaranteed escape.

blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says holding Circle (B on Xbox) while driving ducks behind the wheel to get past police unnoticed; IGN says ducking in a parked car helps you hide at two stars.||
