blocks.title: They go to the scene
blocks.text: Without a description, police head for where the crime happened. In the demo's store robbery, Nelson expects officers to gather out front, and leaves by a back door.

blocks.title: You can stand and fight
blocks.text: Nelson says you can stay and fight the police if you want to. ||PowerPyx says police helicopters break off when shot at, and GameSpot says the pilot announces the retreat over the police radio.||

blocks.title: Chases in missions
blocks.text: Where a mission turns into a chase or a robbery, Rockstar says it tries to keep it consistent with how those systems work in the open world. Your partner can drive while you deal with pursuers.

blocks.title: Patrol car equipment
blocks.text: Before launch, one creator believed police cars carry shotguns or rifles in the trunk, and sometimes body armor. ||Launch guides confirm it. Sportskeeda says the Slim Jim opens a parked police car's door and sitting inside switches off the trunk alarm; it found assault rifles, a shotgun, ammunition, a stun gun, and sometimes money and body armor. PC Gamer says the crate in the bed of a police pickup opens with no alarm at all.||

blocks.title: Cars, a boat and a helicopter
blocks.text: One official screenshot shows patrol cars on a bridge, a boat with flashing police lights on the water below and a helicopter sweeping a searchlight. ||The Wanted Level page lists what launch guides say arrives at each star.||

blocks.title: Who they will not arrest
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx and IGN say that once a character's criminal profile falls to Psycho or Irredeemable, police will not accept surrender, and PowerPyx says they may shoot on sight.||

blocks.title: The getaway car comes first
blocks.text: ||IGN says police who arrive after a reported crime may make impounding the getaway car their first priority.||

blocks.text: Losing
Before launch, the creator TGG described flashing stars, two search circles and a perimeter outside a robbed store. ||Launch guides now describe how a chase ends at each level.||

blocks.caption: Jason leans a sport motorbike into a turn at night, a police car and helicopter behind him.

blocks.title: Break line of sight and hide
blocks.text: Nelson described one star as not a big deal: leave the area and you should be fine. ||IGN says breaking line of sight and hiding ends a one-star response quickly.||

blocks.title: Get out of both zones
blocks.text: TGG reported a darker red search area inside a lighter one, and said getting outside both helps. ||PowerPyx confirms a flashing red and blue search area inside a larger red heat zone, and says its escape trophies only unlock on leaving the red zone or using a Pay 'n' Spray. DayOne says higher levels take longer away from the area to clear.||

blocks.title: Respray the car
blocks.text: TGG reported that a respray removes the description of your car. ||PowerPyx confirms it, with a condition: repainting at a Pay 'n' Spray removes the vehicle's Heat once you are outside the immediate search area.||

blocks.title: Deal with the helicopter
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says police helicopters break off when shot at. IGN says the police scanner tells you when a helicopter leaves to refuel.||

blocks.title: Five stars takes time
blocks.text: ||IGN calls five stars the highest level that can still be escaped, followed by a long search from the air. GameSpot says reaching five is followed by a warning that six will follow, and that a further 10 to 15 minutes of evasion is needed to get away.||

blocks.title: Six stars cannot be lost
blocks.text: Nelson told TGG that at six stars the police search the whole map, and Rockstar would not say what else happens. ||Launch guides agree it cannot be shaken: IGN says it ends only in death or reloading a save, GamesRadar+ that there is no way to resolve it, and DayOne that the Army covers the map until the character is killed. GamesRadar+ says the cheat that raises the wanted level stops at five.||

Three preview details are not covered by the launch guides read: that the depth and clarity of water affect whether police see you underwater, that police set up a perimeter outside a robbed store, and Edge magazine's report of a spike strip stopping Jason's motorbike. ||IGN does confirm K9 units following a suspect on foot from three stars.||

items: Flashing white stars, reported by TGG for a broken line of sight. ||IGN's launch guide does not list them.||
How long the lower levels take to clear. ||The only timings in the guides read are GameSpot's, for five and six stars.||

blocks.text: Busted, wasted
Before launch, TGG reported that Nelson described a busted screen and a respawn, and that banked money is safe while cash on you can be lost. ||Launch guides describe what a failed escape costs.||

blocks.title: Tasers first
blocks.text: ||IGN says one-star police usually carry Tasers that drain stamina, and that police with eyes on an unarmed suspect often use them.||

blocks.title: What you lose
blocks.text: ||Guides agree that being Wasted or Busted costs all the cash you carry, any stash bags, weapons you picked up rather than bought, and vehicles you had not registered. Owned weapons and vehicles are kept. They disagree on the bank: Push Square and IGN's beginner's guide say BuckMe money is safe, while IGN's wanted guide says a small amount comes out of the checking account too. IGN says surrendering costs the same.||

blocks.title: Where the owned guns go
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says owned weapons can be collected again from your personal vehicle's trunk or an Ammu-Nation weapons locker.||

blocks.title: The car is impounded
blocks.text: ||A personal vehicle you were driving when Wasted or Busted is impounded, GamesRadar+ says, and dumping one to clear its Heat will most likely end the same way. GameSpot and GamesRadar+ say stash bags left in it may be lost.||

blocks.title: Getting it back
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says the Scooter Bros app will fetch the car from the impound lot for a large fee, and PowerPyx says Premium credits do it for free. IGN says you can also climb the lot's fence and drive out through the gate for nothing: the police are told only that a vehicle was taken, so a quick exit from the search zone avoids them.||

blocks.title: Check the patrol cars
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says nearby police cars may hold loot already taken from your trunk.||

items: ||A prison sequence. Game Rant says a character who dies respawns nearby; none of the launch guides read describes prison after an arrest.||
||Fines and hospital bills: no guide read gives an amount, and Game Rant mentions hospital fees only as the penalty in earlier games.||
||The impound fee: GamesRadar+ calls it significant but gives no figure.||

blocks.text: Weapon
blocks.sub: What there is, and how it is rated

blocks.text: Before launch Rockstar named only a handful of weapons. Launch guides now sort the arsenal into familiar classes, each with its own place on the weapon wheel.

Rockstar's edition descriptions name Jason's Girardi ES9 and Lucia's Klose K17, both given engraved personal versions in the Ultimate Edition, and the Hawk & Little Morgan revolvers, a pair styled after the Vercetti Estate with palm-tree grips.

blocks.caption: ||The classes as launch guides list them. Game Rant puts pistols in the sidearm slots and shotguns, assault, tactical and sniper rifles in the longarm slots. Prices are story-mode store prices from GTABase, PowerPyx, IGN and Dexerto.||

blocks.title: How many
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx's guide to the Progress database counts 196 weapons: 53 guns, 9 melee weapons, 4 explosives and 130 variants, plus 12 pieces of equipment. IGN agrees on 53 guns, 16 sidearms and 37 longarms, but counts 127 unique variants plus two in the Ultimate Edition.||

blocks.title: Four ratings
blocks.text: ||DayOne publishes each gun's in-game ratings out of 10 for damage, accuracy, handling and range. Jason's ES9 rates 4.2, 5.2, 8.4 and 4.4; the .50-calibre Fairview FF-50 rates 8.5, 7.0, 3.5 and 7.5. TheSixthAxis's review says accessories change a gun's damage and range figures.||

blocks.title: Fire modes
blocks.text: ||DayOne lists semi-automatic, three-round burst (the ES18 pistol, DSG submachine gun and Heathen rifle), fully automatic (including the K17 MCD pistol and KVGA-12 shotgun), pump, break-action and bolt-action guns.||

blocks.title: Attachments and tints
blocks.text: ||GTABase says bought guns can be fitted with attachments and tints, with extended magazines taking the VF5 and KZ-59 to 100 rounds and the M350 machine gun to 200. Unique variants cannot be changed at all (Insider Gaming, IGN).||

blocks.text: Where to
blocks.sub: Ammu-Nation and its unlock rules

blocks.text: Guns, ammunition, armor and parachutes come from Ammu-Nation. What a store stocks depends on its tier, and some guns stay locked until you meet a condition.

blocks.title: Four kinds of store
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 24 gun stores labelled Limited, Standard, Hunting or Expanded. The six Expanded stores carry the widest range, including machine guns, sniper rifles and launchers: Woodhatch, Big Shots, Phil's Ammu-Nation, Black Eagle, Iron & Oak and Prestige Firearms. IGN says only Hunting stores sell the Wortham W-22, and counts 26 locations selling 52 weapons.||

blocks.title: What every store sells
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says every store sells weapons, ammunition, body armor and parachutes and carries at least one unique variant. Map icons show which also have clothing, a weapon locker or fishing rods; IGN says lures, $40 to $112, are sold only at stores showing a fish icon.||

blocks.title: Stock grows
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a store's stock grows with the number of weapons you have bought overall, and that premium stores carry more weapons and exclusive cosmetics.||

blocks.title: The first gun
blocks.text: ||The Chapter 1 mission Gear Up starts at Chuck's Tackle & Shot in Key Lento, where the clerk offers a shotgun or a tactical rifle. IGN mentions the Hawk & Little Mediator at $450 with a first magazine upgrade at $55; Eurogamer suggests first taking another $1,000 from the stash under Jason's bedroom floor to afford attachments. IGN calls the $495 Nipper .38 at Gellhorn Outfitters the cheapest workable pistol.||

blocks.text: Unique
blocks.sub: Named variants and where they turn up

blocks.text: Some guns come with their own name and finish. They cannot be modified, but once found they belong to both leads for good.

blocks.title: How to spot one
blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ and Insider Gaming describe a gold gun icon; IGN calls it yellow, in the world and on the weapon's name in the loadout and locker menus. A unique variant cannot be modified or recoloured, unlocks for Jason and Lucia together, and is not needed for 100% (PowerPyx).||

blocks.title: Raided
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says gang operations usually hold a unique variant among their key valuables. The Gutterball Moreland 850 lies on a table in Kingpin Bowling, Port Gellhorn; IGN places the Kingfishers Akulus at Sunrise RV Park and the Guardia Brothers FRA at Casa Guardia.||

Opening the practice safe at the end of the Chapter 3 mission Safe Word gives Gil's Kalinga .50 and $1,500. blocks.text: In translation, Nelson said long guns can no longer be hidden: one on your back draws little reaction, one in your hands makes people leave or turn hostile. ||Game Rant says only one longarm fits on the back, so a second is carried in the hands. blocks.text: ||GamesRadar+ says a gun bought or given in a mission is owned, and both leads get a copy to modify separately. blocks.title: More than one way to end it
blocks.text: Nelson says a situation can be handled by threatening, knocking someone out, shooting to incapacitate, or killing. In his demo, aiming a gun without firing made the people he had angered run. ||Push Square's review of the released game says enemies can be put down by shots to non-vital areas.||

blocks.title: The yellow X
blocks.text: A yellow X when you hit someone means they are down and will not get back up.
TGG reports three hit markers: white for a hit, yellow for incapacitated, red for a kill.

blocks.title: Long guns show
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson says long guns can no longer be hidden. One on your back draws little reaction; one in your hands makes people leave or turn hostile, and the police warn you first. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it for the released game: everything you carry is visible on the character, and police grow suspicious of long guns.||

blocks.title: Where your guns are kept
blocks.text: Nelson says every weapon you have bought is always available in the back of your personal vehicle. In translation, he adds that Ammu-Nation has lockers where your guns can be collected. ||TheSixthAxis's review agrees: weapons can be kept in weapon lockers or in vehicles you own. PowerPyx's guides place the lockers at Ammu-Nation.||

blocks.title: Firing to frighten
blocks.text: In translation, Nelson describes shooting near a person, not at them, to frighten or confuse them and buy time to get away.

blocks.title: Focus
blocks.text: Nelson compares Focus to Eagle Eye. TGG relays him as saying it can slow combat down. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus works throughout the released game: it highlights valuables, shows enemies in nearby rooms and reveals weak spots in a fight. Push Square's review describes a bullet-time mechanic.||

items: Cover, beyond the fact that it exists. ||Push Square's review says only that cover shooting is improved.||

||Silenced weapons. Melee weapons and explosives are confirmed: TheSixthAxis's review says each lead carries one melee weapon and explosives, PowerPyx's guide to the Progress database counts 9 melee weapons and 4 explosives, and its guides describe sticky bombs sold at Ammu-Nation. TheSixthAxis's review says accessories change a gun's damage and range figures; no launch source read names a silencer.||

blocks.text: Carrying and
What fits on the weapon wheel and how a fight plays, from TGG's account of the preview.

blocks.title: Two and two
blocks.text: Two handguns and two long guns. One long gun goes on your back; a second stays in your hands, where people can see it. ||TheSixthAxis's review gives the full loadout for the released game: two sidearms, two long guns, explosives, one melee weapon and equipment, all of it visible on the character.||

blocks.title: Kept and lost
blocks.text: Your loadout stays with your personal vehicle. Weapons you bought can be recovered. Ones you only picked up can be gone for good. ||TheSixthAxis's review confirms it: weapons can be kept in weapon lockers or in vehicles you own, and a weapon picked up in the world is lost when you quit unless it has been stored.||

blocks.title: The rest of the wheel
blocks.text: Melee weapons, gadgets and throwables have their own room, and items such as healing have a separate tab. ||TheSixthAxis's review lists explosives, one melee weapon and equipment alongside the guns. PowerPyx's guides speak of a weapon wheel, where binoculars are picked, and an item wheel, where body armor is switched on.||

blocks.title: Focus in a fight
blocks.text: Aim at a red area for a lethal shot or a yellow one to incapacitate. You still aim and fire yourself. ||TheSixthAxis's review says Focus reveals weak spots in a fight.||

blocks.title: Recoil
blocks.text: Automatic weapons kick: Nelson fired in short bursts. Pistols fire faster than in Grand Theft Auto V.

blocks.title: Hand to hand
blocks.text: Blocking, dodging and grappling. TGG relays other previews that a block can be held or a parry timed.

items: ||Ammunition: how much can be carried. PowerPyx's launch guide says every gun store sells it.||

chapters.title: Collectibles & Challenges
chapters.intro: What the released game asks you to find, scan, jump, dive for and finish, and how it keeps count. Nearly all of it comes from guides written in launch week, so details are covered until you choose to see spoilers. Every item has its own entry in the Encyclopedia.

blocks.text: Keeping
The game keeps its own record of what you have found. Guides written in launch week counted what that record holds and what 100 percent asks for, and they do not always agree.

blocks.title: The Progress menu
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says the game keeps its own record of what you have found, opened from the map under Progress, and puts it at about 3,000 things. Collections sit under Progress, Collections; Push Square names Kenton's Treasures and Exploration among its tabs. PowerPyx says some groups only appear once you have found something in them, so the counts may not be final.||
blocks.frameAlt: The Progress, Collections screen showing the Vice City Flamingos card set with its card slots

blocks.title: The 100% menu waits for the story
blocks.text: ||IGN says progress toward 100 percent only shows in the game, under Progress, Stats, 100% Completion on the map, once the story is finished. Polygon says that until then the percentage on a save rises only with story missions, by a little under 1 percent each; when the 100% menu unlocked after the story, its save dropped to 66 percent and rose only 2 points in 10 further hours.||

blocks.title: Scanning with WAiNK
blocks.text: ||Many collections are scanned with the phone rather than picked up. IGN says a WAiNK scan is made on foot by holding Up on the D-pad and pressing R1/RB when the prompt appears, and that the controller pulses on its left or right side when a scan is nearby, to show which way it lies from the camera.||

blocks.caption: What there is, and what 100% asks for (PowerPyx and IGN, launch week)
rows: ||This Was No Boat Accident: his final mission||
||Fair Game: a unique animal for Bret||

blocks.text: ||The figures are PowerPyx's unless marked. Where the guides differ: PowerPyx counts 23 No Flusher tags where IGN counts 15, and GameTrek counts 112 WAiNK locations to IGN's 108; IGN counts 5 Kenton sets, one per shipwreck, where PowerPyx describes seven. Reaching 100 percent earns the gold trophy A Long Road.||

blocks.title: Two things to do in Chapter 1
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx flags the meditation at Jason's house as missable: it can only be done in Chapter 1, and Positive Mental Attitude asks for every spot. Its reading guide also marks Jason's house as a missable place to read Ashes of Glory, though that item can be read elsewhere.||
Collectible
How the card sets work, where cards turn up, and what they are worth.

blocks.title: Where cards turn up
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says cards are picked up around the world: indoors on surfaces or stuck to walls, outdoors usually in yellow phone boxes or on tool boxes. They cannot be bought, so the supply is fixed.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia on a La Perle rooftop beside a card, circled, lying on a ledge next to a deck chair

blocks.title: Colour variants count separately
blocks.text: ||Some cards come in colour variants, and each variant counts as its own card (PowerPyx). For the Vice City Flamingos set IGN names Bronze, Gold, Light Blue, Pink, Silver and Standard finishes.||

blocks.title: Keep them or sell them
blocks.text: ||IGN says cards can be kept in a box at the safehouse and sold at any pawn shop, where a card's colour and rarity decide its price. PowerPyx puts that at about $20 to more than $1,000, and says a sold card still counts as collected.||

blocks.title: How many you need
blocks.text: ||The silver trophy Don't Touch My Deck is earned at three complete sets. The 100% checklist asks for 15 of the 18 sets, which PowerPyx works out as at least 372 of the 480 cards. The Exploration challenge Collectible Cards asks for 3 cards in each of the 5 counties.||

blocks.caption: The 18 sets, with IGN’s kind for each

blocks.text: ||Set names follow PowerPyx. IGN calls the Liberty City Swingers set Liberty Swingers, the wrestling set B.A.M. Backyard Wrestling and the comic set Ed Universe. Every card has its own Encyclopedia entry with IGN's directions.||
WAiNK
The phone’s WAiNK app turns landmarks, oddities and street art into collections. Some count toward the 100 scans the checklist wants and some do not.

blocks.title: Five kinds count
blocks.text: ||IGN counts 108 WAiNK locations in five kinds: 31 landmarks, 35 curiosities, 23 sculptures, 4 Pee-Wee billboards and 15 No Flusher tags, and says only these five kinds count among WAiNK scans. PowerPyx's Progress database gives 31 landmarks, 35 curiosities, 23 sculptures and 23 No Flusher tags, with one more kind still unnamed when it was written. You WAiNKer! and the 100% checklist both ask for 100.||
blocks.frameAlt: The Fingerpost signpost among the trees

blocks.title: Landmarks, curiosities and sculptures
blocks.text: ||Examples from the guides: Old Goliath, a giant tree in north-western Ambrosia, is a landmark; the Anti Sugar Residence, a lone house in a construction area west of Ambrosia, is a curiosity; Leonida Snow, in a park in south-eastern Downtown, is a sculpture. The Fingerpost, a signpost pointing to Liberty City on an island in Permit Keys, is a curiosity. The Exploration challenge WAiNK Locations asks for any 4 of these three kinds.||

blocks.title: Pee-Wee billboards
blocks.text: ||IGN counts four Pee-Wee billboards, huge roadside adverts, one each in Vice-Dale, Mariana, Lummox and Leonard counties.||

blocks.title: No Flusher tags
blocks.text: ||Small spray-painted markings on the ground, tied to a toilet-themed group. Push Square says Cal first texts the player about them. IGN places its 15 in Washington Beach, Ocean Beach and Oldby Island; PowerPyx and GameTrek count 23. PowerPyx says the Progress menu shows only how many have been scanned, not which ones.||
blocks.frameAlt: A No Flusher marking on the Shore Dr pavement in Ocean Beach

blocks.title: Scans that do not count
blocks.text: ||AHOL's street art, called Geographies of Trash, is scanned the same way but has its own part of the Collections menu: 112 pieces in 11 kinds, from 15 containers to 7 armchairs. The five 1010 murals are the same. PowerPyx says neither counts toward the 100 WAiNK scans; IGN says scanning all 112 AHOL pieces completes that collection.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason beside a stack of painted tyres in a back lot, IGN's picture for AHOL's Geographies of Trash street art

blocks.title: Posters unlock two playlists
blocks.text: ||Scanning posters unlocks the two unique playlists, both needed for 100%: four posters at Aunt Zola's Soul Food, TWA Ponya Tattoo and Drip Drops in La Perle and the Jack of Hearts club in Crosstown give The Sniper of La Perle, under On Demand; one poster at The Vault nightclub in Downtown gives The Vault Radio, under Radio.||

items: ||Why IGN counts 15 No Flusher tags where PowerPyx and GameTrek count 23, and 108 WAiNK locations where GameTrek counts 112.||
||Which kind PowerPyx's database was still missing when its guide was written; IGN's fifth kind is the Pee-Wee billboards.||

blocks.text: Four kinds of
Stunts are one collection made of four kinds, done by car, bike, plane, helicopter or parachute.

blocks.caption: The four kinds
rows: ||Clear a named ramp; each has a bonus challenge||
||Fly a plane or helicopter beneath a bridge||
||Tip a plane 90 degrees through a gap between buildings||
||A timed parachute jump from a high point, with a par time||

blocks.title: Stunt jumps
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx says every stunt jump has its own name and a small challenge, and that doing the jump is enough for the checklist. IGN gives the bonus challenges, such as landing the Starlet Motel Construction jump with a 2-star wanted level on a Maibatsu Sanchez. PowerPyx's cheats guide makes 50 stunt jumps the requirement for the Unlimited Nitrous cheat.||
blocks.frameAlt: The in-game map with the Exploration, Stunt Jumps list open and the Saltrock Bridge West stunt highlighted

blocks.caption: Stunt jumps and bridges by county

blocks.title: Under the Bridge
blocks.text: ||Flown by plane or helicopter. PowerPyx calls these the quickest stunts to do. PowerPyx and DayOne count 202; IGN's list has 200, among them Leith River South, the bridge between Vinewood Beach and Waning Sands.||

blocks.title: Knife flights
blocks.text: ||A plane is flown on its side through a narrow gap between tall buildings (DayOne). IGN's 40 include the Positano Towers gap in Vice Beach.||
blocks.frameAlt: Tall apartment towers in Vice Beach, IGN's picture for the Positano Towers knife flight

blocks.title: Base jumps
blocks.text: ||IGN says each base jump is a timed run from a high point, such as the top of the Bluegrass antenna mast, with a par time to beat, and that a missed checkpoint adds 10 seconds. DayOne says the game tracks par times beaten, out of 25.||
blocks.frameAlt: Lucia in freefall high above the Vice City skyline

blocks.title: How many you need
blocks.text: ||The silver trophy Cunning Stunts needs 250 stunts of any kind; the 100% checklist needs 300 of the 397.||

blocks.title: Bridges first
blocks.text: ||There are 202 bridges and PowerPyx calls them the quickest stunts, so they are the cheapest way toward the 250 and 300 targets.||
Kenton's
Diving work from Kenton Rees, a treasure hunter in Key Lento, and the other things the sea floor hides.

blocks.title: How it opens
blocks.text: ||Treasure hunting first comes up in the Chapter 1 mission Island Dreams (IGN). Afterwards Kenton, whose jobs carry a green KR icon in Key Lento, adds dive sites to the map as purple chest icons. PowerPyx says he is away for a time after Chapter 1, returns during Chapters 2 to 3, and stays available after the story.||
blocks.frameAlt: Kenton at his counter with the Treasures sale prompt

blocks.title: Gear
blocks.text: ||GameSpot says Island Dreams hands over scuba gear, the Arras Bullhead speargun (the only defence against sharks underwater) and the metal detector, and that Kenton has the gear delivered to another boat if you own one. IGN says any boat taken out for diving needs scuba gear aboard; Kenton's boat and the boat at Jason's safehouse always have it.||

blocks.title: Finding treasure
blocks.text: ||IGN says the metal detector is equipped from the inventory wheel (L1/LB) and aimed with L2/LT; it beeps faster and flashes green near treasure, which is picked up with Triangle (Y). GTA BOOM says one find at Nuestra Señora de la Noche is a separate chest on the seabed with an Open prompt instead of Treasure.||
blocks.frameAlt: A diver on the seabed with the Treasure prompt over the Pewter Gauntlet spot

blocks.title: Doubloons and selling
blocks.text: ||IGN says Kenton pays $400 per doubloon where pawn shops pay $200, and that once a set of sites is cleared some time passes before he texts a new set. Doubloons found away from the first wreck are tracked as sales under Kenton on the Contacts page, which DayOne says also counts shipwrecks cleared, meteorites sold and cash earned.||

blocks.caption: The wrecks (Push Square, GameSpot, IGN)
rows: ||Found during Island Dreams; 10 doubloons clear it. GameSpot spells it del Ocho||
||South-east of the tip of Key Lento||
||Seven treasures, among them the Ivory Saint and the Dragon Pipe||
||South of Key Lento and Abismo Key||
||Five treasures, among them the Ancient Snuff Box||

blocks.title: How many sets
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx describes seven sets and the checklist asks for 5. IGN's treasure page counts 41 treasures at 7 dive sites; its collectibles hub says the first wreck tracks only doubloons and the other six hold 36 unique treasures; its 100% guide counts 5 sets. Kenton's final mission earns This Was No Boat Accident.||
blocks.frameAlt: The sunken wreck of Nuestra Señora del Ocio on the seabed

blocks.title: More on the sea floor
blocks.text: ||The checklist also asks for all 33 Underwater Discoveries, which PowerPyx ties to Kenton's shipwrecks and DayOne's challenge calls unusual sights on the ocean floor. Exploration challenges ask for 85 underwater treasures and all 11 black hole wrecks. Meteorite chunks, found on land and underwater, glow at night (The Big Lead) and sell to Kenton; IGN says they count toward nothing.||

items: ||Whether there are five or seven treasure sets, and 30, 36 or 41 treasures: Push Square, IGN's hub and IGN's treasure page each give a different figure.||
||Where the 33 Underwater Discoveries and the 11 black hole wrecks are: by 18 November no guide read had placed them.||

blocks.text: Flamingos, reading
Smaller collections found around homes, shops and gang hideouts.

blocks.title: Cocaine Flamingos
blocks.text: ||Lawn flamingos that hide cocaine: 125 of them, with 100 needed for 100%. IGN says they are broken open like piñatas, that breaking one fills in the collection page, and that the cocaine can be sold. IGN says the ones that count have a white beak; PowerPyx says a black and white beak, and that they are shot to reveal a package for a fence.||
blocks.frameAlt: A character on a wooden dock standing over a destroyed pink flamingo figure

blocks.title: Magazines, books and comics
blocks.text: ||Twenty-seven readable items, tracked under Progress, Collections, Exploration (Push Square). The guides find them on tables, in sheds and on store magazine racks; Push Square places 11:59 Survivalist Culture up a lookout ladder near Dawson Dam in Mount Kalaga National Park.||
blocks.frameAlt: A character facing a full magazine rack inside a convenience store

blocks.title: Book swaps
blocks.text: ||Seven Little Library boxes each hold a book. IGN numbers them in Watson Bay, Key Lento, Southside, Waning Sands, Ambrosia, Vespucci Island and Capri, and says taking the book and putting it back marks the spot done without reading it. With the 27 reading items they make 34, of which 30 count for 100%.||

blocks.title: Discovered styles
blocks.text: ||Seventy-nine styles in four groups: 13 of Jason's magazine styles, 15 of Lucia's, 17 magazine tattoos and 34 luxury watches. Magazines are scanned with WAiNK; The Big Lead's examples include the Graffiti Point tattoo at the top of the Mount Kalaga fire watch tower. Any 70 count for 100%. No page read says what a style unlocks.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason scanning a magazine on a wooden deck, with a counter reading Jason's Magazine Styles 1 / 13

blocks.title: Luxury watches
blocks.text: ||Watches are picked up, show a golden icon when looked at, and usually sit among the key valuables at gang operations (PowerPyx). IGN names the Crowex Octane 'Orca' as one of the three key valuables at Kingpin Bowling in Port Gellhorn and puts it on a small table by the lanes; PowerPyx places that watch in an office.||
Quiet spots
Meditation spots, Wyman’s project cars, and a few things hidden for their own sake.

blocks.title: Meditation spots
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx counts 18 meditations at 10 spots; most spots count twice, once with each character. The first, at Jason's house with Lucia, can only be done in Chapter 1 and is not marked on the map. The last, at the stone circle on the peak of Mount Kalaga, appears on the map only after all the others. Fifteen count for 100%, Positive Mental Attitude asks for every spot, and TheSixthAxis's review says meditation raises Focus.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason at a lit meditation spot on a rocky beach at night, with the Meditate prompt on screen

blocks.caption: The ten meditation spots (PowerPyx)
rows: ||A sandbar off the west coast of Capri||
||A dock by the lookout tower in Buckskin Swamp||
||The Emerald River bank at Camp Moonflower||
||A ruined paper mill on a river in south Moreau||
||A tower above a mine in Mount Kalaga National Park||
||The stone circle at the peak of Mount Kalaga||

blocks.title: Wyman's cars
blocks.text: Rockstar listed Wyman's Classic Car Collection among the Ultimate Edition's extras: find abandoned classics and unfinished project cars and restore them. ||IGN says it opens after the Chapter 2 mission Thrillbillies. Each wreck is scanned with WAiNK for $50 through BuckMe, and once every wreck of a model is scanned Wyman asks $1,500 for labour before the car can be collected at his scrapyard. The five cars are the '67 Transgressor, '70 Riata, '64 Mamba GT, Reynolds Kit Car and a Deviant. PowerPyx lists them under Exploration but not on its 100% checklist.||
blocks.frameAlt: The in-game map with the Exploration list open on Find Cars for Wyman

blocks.title: Hidden for their own sake
blocks.text: ||GameSpot reports a real egg in a nest on top of the tallest tower in Vice City, which can be taken and thrown; its finder said the climb took about seven minutes. It also points to a western novel about a cowboy in New Austin, a place from the Red Dead series, with one copy in Jacob's Tavern in Millport, and to a Liberty City mob memoir mentioning 2008 on a table in Jason's house early in Chapter 1.||
blocks.frameAlt: The western novel in Jacob's Tavern, Millport

blocks.text: The
Optional goals tracked in the Progress menu, and what finishing them earns.

blocks.title: How they work
blocks.text: ||PowerPyx lists 80 challenges in eight groups of ten, all open from the start. Any 50 earn the bronze trophy One Last Thing and 70 count for 100%. Neither PowerPyx nor DayOne lists a reward for a single challenge.||

blocks.title: Rewards are cheats
blocks.text: ||Finishing five challenges in a group unlocks one vehicle spawn cheat and finishing all ten another. Cheats appear in the Progress menu only after the story, and using one switches off trophies, achievements and saving.||

blocks.caption: The eight groups, with three examples each and their cheats
rows: ||WAiNK Locations, Collectible Cards, Black Hole Wrecks||
||Basketball Rookie, Triple Bank, Double Hole In One||

blocks.title: Exploration and collecting
blocks.text: ||The Exploration group overlaps most with this chapter: scan any 4 WAiNK landmarks, curiosities or sculptures; find 3 cards in each county; discover 100 animals, vehicles and weapons; explore 25 Underwater Discoveries; find 85 underwater treasures and all 11 black hole wrecks; climb to the top of the 5 tallest skyscrapers in Vice-Dale County; and fly over all 41 Vice City and Vice Beach helipads at 100 feet or lower in under 10 minutes.||
blocks.frameAlt: A player at the top of a tall Vice City tower beside a large twig nest holding an egg, with the city below

blocks.title: Where the guides disagree
blocks.text: ||Throttled asks for over 100 mph for 2 minutes in PowerPyx's list and for 2 miles in DayOne's and IGN's. IGN calls the Shopping group High Roller Challenges and the Strength Regime challenge Muscle Regime, and gives Waning Sands Run without PowerPyx's no-damage condition.||

blocks.title: Race challenges are a separate list
blocks.text: ||The 13 race challenges, time trials and stunt runs with bronze, silver and gold medals, are not among the 80; 10 gold medals count for 100%. IGN counts a fourteenth, the supervised Introduction lap with Beau at Gellhorn Raceway.||

chapters.title: Wildlife, Fishing & Hunting
chapters.intro: Leonida’s animals by habitat, the dangerous ones, fishing and hunting. What Rockstar showed before launch is open to read; what players found in the released game is covered until you choose to see spoilers.

blocks.text: Wetlands
Rockstar showed a good deal of Leonida’s wildlife before launch. This page starts with what it showed, then adds what players have found since.

blocks.caption: An airboat in the Grassrivers seen from above, surrounded by alligators.

blocks.title: More than 170 species
blocks.text: Before launch, Game Informer's preview reported more than 170 animal species, native and invasive, and The Guardian's preview that 62 of them are birds, with rare and legendary animals to find. ||PowerPyx counts 255 entries in the game's animal log; the two figures count different things.||

blocks.title: The Grassrivers
blocks.text: Alligators are the Grassrivers' most famous attraction in Rockstar's own description. Red Bull links the manatees in a Rockstar screenshot and diving footage to the Grassrivers' inland waters. Flamingos, spoonbills, pelicans, cranes and ducks were all shown or named before launch.
blocks.frameAlt: A flock of flamingos wading and flying over a wetland

blocks.title: Birds, as players logged them
blocks.text: ||Two Tampa Bay Times environment reporters spent two hours of launch day birding in the game with Florida field guides and counted a dozen species: whooping crane, wood stork, northern gannet, great egret, roseate spoonbill, herring and laughing gulls, Caspian tern, mottled duck, brown and American white pelicans and great blue heron. Audubon Florida's executive director told the paper the spoonbills and white pelicans were locally appropriate.||

blocks.title: The woods of Mount Kalaga
blocks.text: An official Mount Kalaga image shows a cougar stalking deer at a stream. Squirrels, raccoons, otters, beavers, woodpeckers, armadillos, wild boar, rhesus macaques and cane toads were also shown or named before launch. ||Launch guides list the cougar as Cougar/Florida Panther, and Mashable says some hunting challenges send players after a panther.||
blocks.frameAlt: A cougar creeping up on deer drinking from a stream in Mount Kalaga National Park

blocks.caption: Where animals live
rows: ||Alligators, manatees, flamingos, spoonbills, pelicans, cranes, ducks||
||Nile monitor, nutria, round-tailed muskrat, snapping turtle, Leonida cottonmouth, mottled duck, White River Otter||
||American black bear, red and gray foxes, northern coyote, Leonida bobcat, eastern cottontail rabbit, wild turkey, eastern diamondback rattlesnake||
||Dolphins, sharks, whales, jellyfish, eels, sea turtles, stingrays, iguanas||
||American crocodile, hammerhead shark, manta ray, crayfish, blue axanthic iguana||
||Eastern spotted skunk, box turtle, pigeons; rats and possums are disputed||

blocks.text: The grouping is this manual's. Launch-guide animals sit where DayOne's hunting guide or Destructoid's list puts them; pre-launch animals sit where Rockstar's pictures and footage show them, and many live in more than one place.
Coast, sea
The animals of the Keys, the open sea and the streets, from Rockstar’s footage to what players found after launch.

blocks.title: Reefs and open water
blocks.text: An official Leonida Keys image shows divers among coral with a sea turtle, and the Extended Look shows a group of stingrays. Dolphins, sharks, whales, jellyfish and eels were shown or named before launch; Red Bull places dolphins in the open sea and said then that how dangerous sharks would be was not yet known. A red lionfish swims on a Keys reef in Rockstar's launch screenshot gallery.
blocks.frameAlt: Two scuba divers swimming over coral in the Leonida Keys with fish and a sea turtle

blocks.title: Sea animals players found
blocks.text: ||Destructoid and Mashable add hammerhead sharks, manta rays and crayfish, and Destructoid files the American alligator among sea animals. DayOne lists the American crocodile on the coast.||
blocks.frameAlt: A dolphin leaping beside a white speedboat with two people on its rear deck

blocks.title: The Vice City Oceanarium
blocks.text: ||The domed Oceanarium on Catalan Key keeps an orca tank and a dolphin tank; the Vehicle challenge Oceanarium Jump asks for a parachute landing in one of them from half a mile up. TheGamer lists flamingos, manatees and an orca there, and says its writer found the manatees and the orca only at the Oceanarium, which matters for completing the animal log.||

blocks.title: Dogs and cats
blocks.text: Rockstar's Extended Look shows a dog being petted. Official screenshots show a pit bull in a spiked gold collar beside a San4San member and a Carolina dog asleep beside Marabunta Grande members. Cats were named before launch. ||PowerPyx says every dog and cat breed counts separately in the animal log, 34 entries in all. Destructoid and Mashable report Australian shepherds, chihuahuas, Dobermans, German shepherds, Labradors and Rottweilers.||
blocks.frameAlt: A snarling pit bull in a spiked collar on a chain beside its owner

blocks.title: Farm and street animals
blocks.text: ||Destructoid and Mashable both report cows, frogs, herons and pigeons; Mashable adds horses, eagles, storks and cormorants. Destructoid lists rats and possums, but Mashable notes that GTABase lists them while IGN leaves them off, so they are disputed.||
Studying, danger
How the game logs animals, which ones can hurt you, and the few you can get to know.

blocks.title: The animal log
blocks.text: ||The game logs 255 animals in eight groups: 61 hunts, 60 birds, 35 fish, 34 cats and dogs, 18 mammals, 18 aquatic animals, 6 reptiles and 23 others. PowerPyx says each is studied through the binoculars from the weapon wheel, that hunting or skinning is not needed, and that 100 count for the checklist.||
blocks.frameAlt: A wild boar in shaded undergrowth, seen through a rifle scope with its study panel

blocks.title: Challenges for studying
blocks.text: ||The Survival challenge Zoologist asks for 20 species studied, and the Exploration challenge Encyclopedia for 100 animals, vehicles and weapons discovered.||

blocks.title: Animals that fight back
blocks.text: ||Mashable says alligators can eat you, and the Survival challenge Alligator Kills asks for 3 wild ones. GameSpot says the Arras Bullhead speargun from Island Dreams is the only defence against sharks underwater. DayOne groups bears with the larger or more dangerous animals best shot from a distance.||

blocks.title: Bigfoot
blocks.text: ||Launch-week players met a Bigfoot in the swamps south of Hamlet: Insider Gaming says at Cottonmouth Lake, GameSpot says Gullet Marsh, and neither says whether the two are the same area. PowerPyx says it is the creature Kirk hunts as the Skunk Ape or Mr. Mangrove in his Strangers and Freaks missions.||

blocks.title: Petting and pets
blocks.text: Dogs can be petted, as the Extended Look shows. ||Mashable says a dog can be given a treat with its owner's permission. Jason keeps a pet snake, Dolores, in a terrarium near the kitchen of his Key Lento house; Polygon says feeding her gives 3% Focus once a day, and Mashable says she is the only pet Jason can keep in the story.||
blocks.frameAlt: Jason at the snake terrarium with the Feed Dolores prompt, the snake visible in the tank

blocks.title: Animals with names
blocks.text: ||Some animals are one of a kind: Gary, Ms. Sharleen's alligator in a cowboy hat on Calypso Avenue, Key Lento; a Festive Poodle and a Cartoon Labrador to scan at houses in Key Lento; and a dog on a jet ski that may rescue a player left alone in open water, such as Gambit Bay, and lead them to an island with about $1,200 to find. Insider Gaming says the dog digs up a $1,200 stash; Game8 describes a wallet with $1,218 on a body. GameSpot could not make the dog appear in its own test.||
blocks.frameAlt: An alligator wearing a small brown cowboy hat on sandy grass, a woman's hand reaching toward it

blocks.text: Gone
How fishing works, which lure catches what, and the challenges built around it.

blocks.title: The rod
blocks.text: ||IGN says fishing can be done almost anywhere a line can be cast, at any time, with a tutorial in the Chapter 1 mission Recalibration. The rod is always carried, in the same slot as the binoculars and flashlight: hold L1/LB and cycle with L2/LT or R2/RT.||
blocks.frameAlt: A red lionfish on a Leonida Keys reef

blocks.caption: ||Landing a fish, as IGN describes it.||
steps: ||Pick a lure with Left or Right on the D-pad||
||Use Focus to see fish glowing in the water||
||Hold L2/LT to aim and draw back R2/RT to set the cast's strength||
||Reel slowly with the right stick; a light rumble is only a nibble||
||On a stronger shake, press R2/RT to hook the fish||
||Push the left stick against the fish to tire it, then reel fast once the rumbling eases||

blocks.title: Lures
blocks.text: ||Lures are sold only at Ammu-Nations that show a fish icon under Features on the map. Once a species has been caught, its hotspots are marked with a purple fish icon. The Candy Cane Lure is not sold anywhere; IGN found it in a garage of a house in Ambrosia.||

blocks.caption: The 35 fish by lure (IGN)
rows: ||Bluegill, Lake Chubsucker, Largemouth Bass, Redfin Pickerel, Redbreast Sunfish||
||American Eel, Channel Catfish, Leonida Gar, Salt Fish||
||Stoplight Parrotfish, Greater Amberjack, Rock Sea Bass, Bluestriped Grunt, Littlehead Porgy, Yellowtail Snapper||
||Atlantic Spadefish, Striped Bass, Spotted Moray Eel, Black Grouper, Tiger Grouper, Hogfish, Northern Red Snapper, Common Snook, Red Lionfish||
||Atlantic Tarpon, Atlantic Thread Herring, Great Barracuda, Cobia, Green Moray Eel, Mahi Mahi, Permit, Yellowfin Tuna||
||Black Drum (no lure named); Atlantic Spanish Mackerel (a saltwater lure, size not given)||

blocks.text: ||IGN's lure list names Small Freshwater, Medium Freshwater, Medium Saltwater and Large Saltwater lures, yet its fish entries also call for a Small Saltwater Lure, with no price for either small lure. IGN says the 35 fish are listed alphabetically in the Fishing tab of the Progress menu.||

blocks.title: Where to try
blocks.text: ||IGN suggests one spot per species. Freshwater fish come from the Grassrivers, Lake Leonida, Lake Tallaloko, Buckskin Swamp, Gullet Marsh, Cottonmouth Lake and the Emerald and Nehrling rivers; the large saltwater fish from the Leonida Straits off Key Lento, the Atlantic east of Vice Beach and the Gulf of Leonida. Each fish's Encyclopedia entry gives IGN's spot.||
blocks.frameAlt: An eel swimming through blue water near coral

blocks.title: Cal's fishing rivalries
blocks.text: ||Cal texts fishing record challenges that put a purple fish icon on the map. The first, Catch a Bigger Fish, comes after the Chapter 1 mission Feng Shui and asks Jason for a Stoplight Parrotfish over 2 lb in Gambit Bay; Push Square gives the weight as 2 kg. Cross (A) sends Cal a photo of the catch, which earns a Focus increase and the Baited My Tackle trophy. After Chapter 1 the boat at Jason's house is gone; PowerPyx suggests the docks near The Rusty Anchor.||

blocks.title: Fishing challenges and Focus
blocks.text: ||Four Survival challenges involve fishing: Big Fish (20 pounds or more), Catch of the Day (3 fish with each type of lure in a day), Angler (4 species in under 6 minutes) and Pro Angler (every species). IGN says fishing raises Focus and that Focus gains, unlike Strength and Cardio, are permanent.||
Hunting
Hunting as launch guides describe it, and what is still unconfirmed.

blocks.title: Bret Vogel
blocks.text: ||Hunting work comes from Bret Vogel, Jason's old army friend, who runs the Killtelligence business near Mount Kalaga. Only Jason can do it. Some time after the Chapter 2 mission Coffee Break, a text from Bret marks the mission Veteran Hunted in Lummox County, which pays $500 through BuckMe and hands over the unique Killtelligence SM-69 rifle. PowerPyx says unique weapons can be collected again from any Ammu-Nation weapon locker.||
blocks.frameAlt: A bobcat lying on the back of a vehicle beside a person holding a rifle

blocks.title: Target decks
blocks.text: ||After Veteran Hunted, Bret marks hunting spots with purple map icons and asks for particular animals, which Jason brings to him. Progress is tracked under Map, Activities, Target Deck. There are 15 decks, all needed for 100%, and the strand stays open after the story.||
blocks.frameAlt: A whitetail doe standing among trees, seen through a hunting rifle scope

blocks.caption: The first three decks (Push Square's guide, still in progress)
rows: ||Mount Kalaga National Park, Abandoned Concrete Plant||
||Includes the Eastern Spotted Skunk and the Leonida Wild White Tom||
||Adler Creek, Bonanza, Mount Kalaga National Park||
||Includes the Nile Monitor and the Nutria||
||West and East Buckskin Swamp, Pelican Valley||

blocks.title: Clean kills pay more
blocks.text: ||Animals killed with one clean shot stay pristine and pay more, though that is not required (PowerPyx). Smaller kills are bought straight from the car's trunk at Bret's building, while Bret collects large carcasses, such as bears, himself; PC Gamer reports $2,500 for a large boar. Push Square says the skunk, which is nocturnal, appeared after about 8pm in grassy areas, and that Bret accepts only the white-feathered turkey.||
blocks.frameAlt: A white turkey and a darker one in grass, seen through a rifle scope, with a panel naming the Leonida Wild White Tom

blocks.title: Which rifle
blocks.text: ||DayOne recommends the Wortham W-22, a .22 rifle IGN lists in Ammu-Nation's hunting stock only, for small game such as rabbits, squirrels, ducks, turkeys and iguanas; the Hawk & Little Mediator for foxes, coyotes and bobcats; and the Shrewsbury SM-69 for alligators, crocodiles, black bears and wild boar. PowerPyx says the Shrewsbury SMS-01 goes on sale only after Bret's ninth hunting job.||

blocks.title: Unique and rare animals
blocks.text: ||The game has 8 unique animals: the Survival challenge Legendary Hunter asks for all of them, and the Fair Game trophy for hunting one for Bret. Hunting Spree asks for a boar, a rattlesnake and a panther in under 15 minutes without taking damage from enemies or animals. Rare colour forms in DayOne's list include the Piebald Whitetail Buck, Mosaic Mottled Duck, Blue Axanthic Iguana and White River Otter.||

blocks.title: Practice
blocks.text: ||The Rodgers Ranch Hunting Range, north-east of Port Gellhorn, is a score course with small animals as targets and four tiers; PowerPyx says animal heads score the same as the red weak points. The arcade game Bang For Your Buck is a light-gun hunting game that, Press Start says, rewards shooting bucks while sparing does.||
